E.1

We deploy JARVIS-VLA with its action-token decoder and two history entries to predict one action per decision.

UI-TARS-1.5-7B uses three previous screenshots, deterministic decoding, and a 400-token output limit. Its adapter maps pixel-coordinate actions to one benchmark interval, with drag and double-click unsupported.

NitroGen aggregates an 18-action chunk into six benchmark decisions (three native actions per decision), refreshing the image after each chunk.

GameWAM predicts 16 actions and executes eight before replanning, using its Minecraft checkpoint outside Doom and its ViZDoom checkpoint for Doom.

Open-P2P uses visual-only conditioning and session-specific recurrent state.

All temporal inference state is isolated between episodes.

Model inputs retain the released preprocessing for the best practice of each baseline: Minecraft is rendered at $864\times 480$ . We resize the screenshots to $640\times 360$ for JARVIS-VLA and UI-TARS, $256\times 256$ for NitroGen, $224\times 224$ for GameWAM, and $192\times 192$ for Open-P2P.

JARVIS-VLA and GameWAM retain their native degree-based Minecraft camera actions, while Open-P2P uses an adapter gain of $0.15$ degrees per raw mouse pixel.

Browser-game adapters project native actions onto per-game and per-role bindings.

Benchmark action intervals remain fixed, so a native action chunk can span different simulated durations across benchmarks.

item.title: DashVMC：活游戏里的实时世界模型控制 ｜ DashVMC: Real-Time Discrete World Model Control in Geometry Dash
item.description:
一句话：只用约 2 小时录像学世界模型，在消费级 GPU 上维持 60Hz 的「截帧→预测→动作」闭环。

要点：

  • 从约 2 小时的 Geometry Dash 录像里学紧凑的动作条件世界模型，每个动作预测 64 token 的下一帧网格
  • 控制器先行为克隆，再完全在冻结模型的 rollout 里用 PPO 精修，不再与活游戏交互
  • 部署时跳过视觉生成，在消费级 GPU 上维持 60Hz 的采集到动作闭环；三个控制器种子在三个官图与一张社区图上都活得更久

为什么值得看：活游戏不能等策略——这篇把「不暂停、不降帧」作为硬约束，给出了世界模型在线控制的可行落地形态。

中文摘要：世界模型智能体通常在可以等策略的模拟器里评测，而活游戏施加的约束正相反：必须在下一帧到来前完成采集、预测与动作。DashVMC 从约两小时的 Geometry Dash 录像中学习一个紧凑的、以动作为条件的世界模型，每步预测 64 token 的下一帧离散网格。为了验证学到的动力学是否真的可用，控制器先用行为克隆初始化，再完全在冻结世界模型的 rollout 里用 PPO 精修，全程不再与活游戏交互。三个随机种子的精修策略在三个官方关卡与一张留出的社区布局上，存活时间都超过行为克隆初始版本。部署阶段它干脆跳过视觉生成，在消费级 GPU 上维持 60Hz 的采集到动作回路，说明即便长程保真度不完美，这种表示仍足以支撑控制。

主题：AI Native Engine

来源：arXiv·cs.LG（English）

License: CC BY 4.0

arXiv:2609.40003v1 [cs.LG] 30 Sep 2026\metadata

[Project page][Code]

tariolle.github.io/dash-vmc

\metadata

github.com/Tariolle/dash-vmc

\correspondence

DashVMC

Abstract

World-model agents are usually evaluated in simulators that can wait for the policy; live games impose the opposite constraint, requiring capture, prediction, and action before the next frame.

We present , which learns a compact, action-conditioned world model from approximately two hours of recorded Geometry Dash gameplay.

To test whether the learned dynamics are actionable, a controller is initialized by behavioural cloning (BC) and refined with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) entirely in frozen-model rollouts, without further interaction with the live game.

Across three controller seeds, the refined policies survive longer than their BC initializations on all three official levels and a held-out community layout.

At deployment, the baseline skips visual generation and sustains a 60-Hz capture-to-action loop on a consumer GPU.

Action-conditioned continuations and rollout diagnostics show that the model remains useful for control despite imperfect long-horizon fidelity.DashVMC

1

A world model learns transition dynamics $p_{\theta}(s_{t+1}\mid s_{t},a_{t})$ and can be rolled forward so that an agent practices without further environment interaction .

DashVMC asks whether such practice can improve a policy that must then act in a live, non-paused game.

It predicts a 64-token next grid in parallel for inexpensive imagined rollouts.

The baseline deployment skips generation and reuses the transformer’s temporal summary; a matched ablation tests whether the transformer must remain in the live loop.(; )

LeCun, 2022

Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018

Most world-model agents are evaluated in synchronous environments that wait for the policy.

A live, non-paused application reverses that contract: screen capture, perception, inference, and action dispatch must finish before the action becomes stale.

Geometry Dash is a small but unforgiving test of this contract.

The avatar moves continuously, the action space is binary, and a mistimed jump causes immediate death.

Levels are deterministic, but the agent observes only captured pixels and acts through keyboard events; it does not receive emulator state during control.

The apparent simplicity therefore isolates a demanding question: can an agent learn when to act from pixels, improve without touching the live game, and still react within narrow timing windows on modest hardware?

DashVMC follows the perception–dynamics–control organization of World Models : it compresses each frame into a discrete grid, learns action-conditioned grid dynamics, initializes a lightweight action model with BC, and refines it with PPO in the frozen model.()

Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018

()

Schulman et al., 2017

Our contributions are:

1.

a compact discrete, action-conditioned world model learned from approximately two hours of offline gameplay, whose rollouts support policy refinement without further live-game interaction;

2.

a decoder-free baseline that sustains a 60-Hz capture-to-action loop on a consumer GPU, together with a spatial-only variant that removes the transformer at inference without a consistent live-performance deficit; and

3.

evidence that the learned dynamics are actionable: controllers refined only in frozen-model rollouts improve over their exact BC parents on all three official levels across three seeds and on a held-out layout.

Diagnostics cover action sensitivity, rollout fidelity, controller input, dynamics losses, and latency.

2

World models and imagination.

World Models demonstrated that a compact controller optimized in learned dreams can transfer to the real environment .

IRIS combines a discrete autoencoder with an autoregressive transformer for data-efficient Atari learning ; $\Delta$ -IRIS reduces sequence cost with discrete delta tokens and continuous context tokens ; DIAMOND uses diffusion for imagination-trained control ; and DreamerV3 scales categorical recurrent latents across domains .

TWISTER adds action-conditioned CPC to transformer dynamics , which DashVMC adopts alongside parallel spatial prediction.

Earlier screenshot-based Geometry Dash control used DQN and imitation under a fabricated timestep ; here the game clock continues during capture and inference.()

Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018

()

Micheli et al., 2023

()

Micheli et al., 2024

()

Alonso et al., 2024

()

Hafner et al., 2025

()

Burchi and Timofte, 2025

()

Li and Rafferty, 2017

FSQ tokenization and policy initialization.

FSQ replaces learned vector-quantization codebooks with bounded scalar levels, avoiding commitment losses and codebook collapse while exposing an integer coordinate lattice ; we use the improved iFSQ bounding function .

Demonstration-based RL can reduce costly early exploration ; here recorded actions initialize the controller, while the retained policy is selected only after imagined PPO refinement.

Deterministic Sobel preprocessing removes appearance detail before tokenization, providing a compact task-specific alternative to richer continuous or generative representations.()

Mentzer et al., 2024

()

Lin et al., 2026

(; )

Hester et al., 2018

Baker et al., 2022

3

DashVMC is organized around a simple loop: recorded play trains a world model, the action model is refined in rollouts from the frozen dynamics model, and the resulting controller is returned to the live game.

The visual encoder, dynamics model, and action model are trained in sequence and then frozen for deployment.

Figure shows how the same learned state supports both imagined practice and live reaction.

1

: Figure 1Learning in imagination and acting in the live game. A recorded context seeds the frozen world model; the action model chooses what to do, the world model predicts the consequence, and PPO updates only the action model. In the baseline live path, the encoder and temporal context provide the state used for action selection, while visual generation is skipped.(a)(b)

3.1

Each RGB capture is cropped, converted to grayscale, filtered with Sobel edges, and resized to $64\times 64$ .

A convolutional autoencoder maps the result through three stride-2 stages to a four-channel $8\times 8$ latent map.

Each spatial vector is independently quantized with iFSQ levels $[8,5,5,5]$ , using the bounding function $2\operatorname{sigmoid}(1.6z)-1$ , and yields $64$ token IDs from $1000$ implicit codes .

The tokenizer is trained on adjacent frames with reconstruction, temporal-slowness, and latent-uniformity objectives .

Once selected, its encoder is frozen; its decoder is used to visualize dreams but is not required by the action model.(; )

Mentzer et al., 2024

Lin et al., 2026

()

Xia et al., 2025

3.2

The dynamics model is an eight-layer, width-384 transformer that receives four recent frame–action pairs.

Each frame block contains 64 visual tokens and one / status token, with action tokens inserted between blocks; a final masked block requests the next frame.

Attention is bidirectional within a frame and causal across frame/action blocks, so all next-frame positions are predicted in one forward pass without seeing their targets.

An explicit action token separates consecutive frames, so the model can answer the question central to policy learning: what changes if the action model jumps rather than idles?

It predicts all 64 codes of the next grid in parallel, together with an / score, and exposes a temporal summary $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ , taken from the most recent action-token position, to the action model.

Parallel prediction keeps imagined steps inexpensive.alivedeathalivedeath

Training combines next-grid prediction with action-conditional contrastive predictive coding of weight 0.1 , context corruption, and an auxiliary death objective.

For context corruption, 5% of context tokens are replaced uniformly and another 5% with adjacent FSQ codes.

The token loss uses focal modulation and structured label smoothing (SLS): for target lattice coordinate $\mathbf{c}_{i}$ , smoothing mass $\varepsilon=0.1$ is distributed over non-target codes proportionally to $\exp(-\|\mathbf{c}_{i}-\mathbf{c}_{j}\|_{2}^{2}/2\sigma^{2})$ , with $\sigma=0.9$ .

Focal modulation is applied once to the aggregate soft-target cross-entropy, and the output projection is tied to the token embedding.(; )

Burchi and Timofte, 2025

van den Oord et al., 2018

()

Lin et al., 2017

3.3

The $45{,}546$ -parameter actor–critic embeds the current token grid, processes it with two convolutions and max pooling, and concatenates the resulting 256-dimensional feature with the dynamics model’s temporal summary $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ .

Separate heads predict jump probability, value, and an eight-action auxiliary output covering the current and next seven actions.

The matched spatial-only ablation removes $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ from BC, PPO, and deployment, leaving a 41,706-parameter action model; the world model still generates its PPO rollouts.

BC first reproduces recorded action timing; PPO then departs from imitation through repeated imagined consequences.

Each PPO iteration generates 512 imagined episodes of at most 45 steps from recorded four-frame contexts, with greedy next-grid predictions and sampled Bernoulli actions.

The first four generated transitions refresh the context but are excluded because the recorded approach may make collision unavoidable; the remainder covers visible obstacles before invented geometry dominates.

Rollouts terminate when the death logit exceeds the logit; because death frames are oversampled $5\times$ , this is an operational boundary rather than a calibrated probability.

Reward is $+1$ per survived step and $-0.25$ per jump, discouraging a local optimum in which an early jump merely delays collision while airborne and earns extra survival reward without clearing the obstacle.

We use Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) with $\gamma=0.995$ , $\lambda=0.95$ , PPO clip 0.2, and auxiliary-action loss weight 0.1.alive()

Schulman et al., 2015

3.4

Training generates consequences; baseline live control only interprets recent observations.

Desktop Duplication captures only the $1032\times 1032$ model crop; CPU grayscale conversion followed by CUDA Sobel filtering and area resizing produces the $64\times 64$ observation.

Each frame is encoded and appended to a GPU-resident context, and the transformer runs context prefill only to produce $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ .

The live context marks every observation ; process-memory death detection only terminates and restarts an attempt outside the controller.

The next-grid predictor and image decoder are skipped, reducing the deployed path to 15.57 million parameters; the encoder uses , and transformer context encoding uses a CUDA Graph after warm-up.

The accelerated preprocessing path was checked against the recorded-data pipeline on synthetic and fresh live captures and produced byte-identical observations.

Spatial-only deployment loads only the frozen encoder and action model; both paths are reactive controllers whose policy improvement occurred during offline imagined training.alivetorch.compile

4

Data and training.

Before augmentation, the corpus contains 4,264 action-labelled gameplay episodes, or 251,963 frames and approximately 2.33 hours at the nominal 30-FPS capture cadence.

It includes deliberate failures, official Levels 1–7, several community levels, and 36 expert trajectories or segments totaling less than 20 minutes.

BC uses action labels from both the deliberate-failure and expert corpora.

Recording samples the current key state after each capture; deployment appends the new capture with the previously held state before dispatching the next, while process memory only segments deaths and restarts.

Mechanics outside the selected scope, including gravity inversion, are excluded.

Failure and expert trajectories are each split 90/10 with seed 42 at the base-episode level.

During tokenizer training, each adjacent-frame pair receives a shared two-dimensional translation whose horizontal and vertical offsets are sampled independently and uniformly from $[-4,4]$ pixels.

For dynamics training, the frozen encoder instead tokenizes each base episode at vertical offsets $\{-4,-2,0,2,4\}$ , expanding the corpus to 21,320 episode variants.

All windows and variants inherit their base-episode assignment; although no complete trajectories are duplicated, deterministic repeated attempts can share near-identical prefixes, so the 10% stratum is an in-distribution development set rather than a generalization test.

The tokenizer, dynamics model, and BC controller use this split; PPO draws rollout seeds from the full corpus and uses 512 fixed development contexts for checkpoint selection.

Tokenizer and dynamics training use seed 42, while controller training is repeated with seeds 43–45 under the same frozen representation and world model.

The first two stages run sequentially in BF16 on one A100, controller training runs in BF16 on one H200, and live inference and local latency evaluation use the same RTX 2060 with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu126 (CUDA 12.6).

: Table 1Training and checkpoint selection; tokenizer/dynamics learning rates use cosine decay.

The retained full runs took 3.19 A100 hours for the tokenizer, 4.20 A100 hours for the dynamics model, and 17.41 H200 hours for the seed-43 $H=45$ controller, including BC and 15,000 PPO iterations.

Thus the retained pipeline required 24.80 hours of sequential training while occupying one GPU at a time—roughly one day end to end.

The matched spatial-only controller took 17.12 H200 hours under the same iteration budget.

Checkpoint and live evaluation.

PPO checkpoint selection uses survival on 512 fixed latent development contexts every ten iterations.

All live checkpoints are then frozen and act deterministically from pixels alone; Auto-Retry standardizes restarts but provides no policy input.

For each seed, we compare PPO with the exact BC checkpoint that initialized it over 25 scored attempts on , , and .

BC and PPO attempts are separate samples paired only by lineage and run until detected death.

Background appearance cycles independently of level progress, while capture and dispatch phases vary near timing boundaries; repetitions measure this pixel-level deployment variability.

The protocol also covers , which begins at Level 1’s first ship section, and post-freeze community layout , a held-out test within supported mechanics.

To validate the earlier 30-FPS evaluations, a cadence check compares the identical frozen PPO checkpoint on Stereo Madness Copy over 25 optimized-path attempts at 60 FPS and 20 earlier diagnostic-path attempts at 30 FPS.Stereo MadnessBack on TrackPolargeistStereo Madness CopyStereo INSANE Nerfed

The endpoint is frames survived, except the cross-cadence probe uses wall time.

PPO-minus-BC intervals independently resample each frozen policy’s 25 attempts 50,000 times and characterize deployment variability; the three seed differences provide replication.

A post-freeze probe retrains seed 43 from the same BC parent with $H=20$ for 30,000 iterations (15.61 H200 hours), versus $H=45$ for 15,000 (17.41 hours), and scores 10 versus 25 attempts per layout.

Because horizon and iteration count co-vary, this is a roughly compute-matched shorter-rollout probe, not an isolated ablation.

A second seed-43 probe keeps the $H=45$ recipe and 15,000-iteration budget but removes $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ from controller training and inference.

It scores the resulting BC and PPO checkpoints over 10 attempts on the three official levels and held-out layout; comparisons with the 25-attempt temporal-state reference independently bootstrap the two frozen-policy samples.

Latency and continuation protocols.

Live latency covers capture through dispatch over 5,000 optimized-path frames.

The qualitative intervention starts immediately before a spike from one encoded four-frame prefix; greedy branches differ only in their first action and then idle.

Quantitative diagnostics re-encode the unaugmented development trajectories, yielding 22,745 next-frame windows from 413 usable trajectories.

The paired intervention flips only the final context action and bootstraps trajectories 5,000 times; autoregressive diagnostics greedily feed predictions back while replaying recorded actions.

The standard cohort has 1,024 starts from 153 trajectories; the exploratory 200-step cohort has 256 starts from the only four sufficiently long trajectories.

Targeted dynamics-loss ablations.

We compare the reported structured-SLS+CPC dynamics model with three single-training-run variants: uniform label smoothing with the same $\varepsilon=0.1$ , no label smoothing, and structured SLS without CPC.

They retain the tokenizer, corpus, split, architecture, seed 42, optimization, and maximum-development-death-F1 selection rule; all checkpoints share the exact evaluation windows and rollout starts.

External transition-latency protocol.

We also time the native imagined transition of DashVMC and released Pong checkpoints of IRIS and DIAMOND on the same RTX 2060.

Each runs in a fresh process at batch one with FP32 eager execution for 30 warm-ups and two repetitions of 100 synchronized transitions; differing native interfaces make this a cost, not quality, comparison.

5

5.1

The central question is whether policy improvement learned only through frozen-model rollouts transfers beyond imitation to the live game.

The selected tokenizer reconstructs development edge maps at 34.10 dB PSNR, and the dynamics model reaches 29.58% visual-token accuracy.

Deaths comprise 1.80% of its 22,745 development windows; at threshold 0.5 the death head obtains 0.721 precision, 0.883 recall, 0.794 F1, 0.994 AUROC, and 0.050 expected calibration error.

Because this stratum selected the dynamics checkpoint, these are in-distribution development diagnostics rather than untouched test results.

These component metrics establish a usable but imperfect imagined environment; the live comparison below tests whether it nevertheless teaches better actions.

: Table 2Live survival on all five layouts. No-op entries are mean frames $\pm$ standard deviation over 10 attempts and are shared across seeds. BC/PPO entries use 25 attempts; $\Delta$ is PPO minus its exact parent BC [95% attempt-level bootstrap interval]. The first three are official levels, Stereo Madness Copy begins in ship form, and Stereo INSANE Nerfed is held out.

LevelPolicySeed 43Seed 44Stereo MadnessNo-opshared: $46.2\pm 0.7$ BC $120.2\pm 91.8$ $130.6\pm 76.0$ PPO $\boldsymbol{280.1\pm 23.3}$ $\boldsymbol{280.4\pm 33.5}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $159.9\ [122.7,195.4]$ $149.8\ [116.8,180.6]$ Back on TrackNo-opshared: $63.4\pm 0.7$ BC $123.5\pm 81.5$ $111.1\pm 60.3$ PPO $\boldsymbol{260.0\pm 55.5}$ $\boldsymbol{195.9\pm 126.5}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $136.5\ [98.8,174.4]$ $84.8\ [31.9,139.6]$ PolargeistNo-opshared: $41.5\pm 0.7$ BC $52.4\pm 16.7$ $49.0\pm 16.5$ PPO $\boldsymbol{65.2\pm 33.4}$ $\boldsymbol{68.3\pm 44.1}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $12.8\ [-0.2,28.6]$ $19.4\ [3.0,39.0]$ Stereo Madness CopyNo-opshared: $135.0\pm 0.0$ BC $366.8\pm 172.8$ $285.7\pm 153.5$ PPO $\boldsymbol{435.6\pm 196.1}$ $\boldsymbol{495.8\pm 137.5}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $68.8\ [-33.3,166.1]$ $210.1\ [127.9,285.5]$ Stereo INSANE NerfedNo-opshared: $46.1\pm 0.8$ BC $104.8\pm 72.1$ $102.1\pm 64.0$ PPO $\boldsymbol{290.4\pm 48.6}$ $\boldsymbol{342.8\pm 80.8}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $185.5\ [151.1,217.6]$ $240.6\ [200.8,280.2]$

In Table , BC exceeds no-op everywhere and PPO improves over its parent in all fifteen seed-level comparisons.

Across the three controller seeds, the paired improvements are $154.2\pm 5.2$ frames on , $103.5\pm 28.7$ on , and $16.3\pm 3.3$ on , where the variation is the sample standard deviation across the three seed differences.

Every interval on the first two levels excludes zero; the smaller Polargeist gain is positive for all seeds, but seed 43’s interval marginally includes zero.

Polargeist’s smaller gain may reflect its yellow-orb mechanic, which requires a second, precisely timed jump input while airborne and is absent from the preceding levels.

2

Stereo MadnessBack on TrackPolargeist

On Stereo Madness Copy, seed 43’s interval includes zero but seeds 44–45 exclude it (mean gain $175.4\pm 94.2$ ); on held-out Stereo INSANE Nerfed, all exclude zero (mean gain $198.3\pm 37.6$ ).

The Copy is not held out, but exposes strong altitude control from Level 1’s first ship section.

The 60-FPS cadence probe on Stereo Madness Copy yields similar observed real-time survival: mean recorded episode wall time is 17.72 s at 60 FPS versus 17.79 s at 30 FPS, with a 95% bootstrap interval of $[-1.04,0.89]$  s for the mean difference (60 FPS minus 30 FPS).

This limited one-checkpoint, one-layout probe supports cadence transfer there, not equivalence across the primary cube levels.

Runtime temporal-state ablation.

The matched spatial-only controller gives up 1.11 frames on the fixed dream-selection metric, reaching 29.02/45 versus 30.13/45 for the seed-43 temporal-state reference.

: Table 3Seed-43 controller-input ablation (mean frames $\pm$ sample SD). Dream is best survival on the same 512 fixed contexts; live results use 25 attempts for the temporal-state reference and 10 for spatial-only.

Live performance is largely retained without $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ .

This suggests that temporal state contributes little in this predominantly reactive game, where the current grid exposes nearby geometry and avatar position and recent history mainly disambiguates motion such as scrolling and vertical velocity.

A memory-dependent environment would be expected to show a larger drop when $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ is removed.

Although $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ improves dream-selection survival by 1.11 frames, the world model’s demonstrated role remains to provide PPO’s offline training environment.

5.2

The complete perception-to-action loop must finish within 16.67 ms; at 60 Hz it can revise the binary key state every frame, not press 60 times per second.

While the RTX 2060 also renders the game, 5,000 measurements have mean/median 12.018/12.083 ms, p95 14.068 ms, p99 14.913 ms, and maximum 24.059 ms.

Eleven frames (0.22%) exceed the period; on a miss the loop skips its pacing sleep and immediately begins the next capture rather than reusing an old action.

This doubles the temporal resolution of the 30-FPS demonstrations.

Qualitatively, the ship policy uses sustained thrust and release intervals: ship motion remains correctable in flight, whereas a cube jump is largely ballistic until landing and therefore demands sparser, more precise timing.

The smooth, low-duty-cycle behaviour is consistent with PPO’s per-step jump penalty, although it does not isolate that penalty’s effect.

5.3

DashVMC’s native imagined transition averages 11.05 ms, compared with 49.30 ms for DIAMOND and 177.83 ms for IRIS, corresponding to 4.5 $\times$ and 16.1 $\times$ lower latency, respectively.

Only DashVMC fits the 16.67-ms 60-FPS period on this hardware.

: Table 4Batch-1 native imagined-transition latency on an RTX 2060 (synchronized run means in milliseconds). Interfaces differ, so this compares operational cost rather than quality.

Parallel grid prediction and latent-space feedback avoid autoregressive token generation and pixel decoding at every imagined step, compounding the savings through PPO.

5.4

Beyond its 45-step training horizon, the model feeds predicted grids and new actions back into context.

Interactive rollouts reproduce scrolling terrain, camera and height changes, collisions, and avatar transformations; long continuations may remain coherent or eventually repeat, empty, or invent impossible geometry.

Video demonstrations of interactive level continuations are available on the .

project page

: Table 5Recorded-action rollout diagnostics. Accuracy and decoder-space PSNR compare predicted with recorded grids; JS compares pooled token marginals. Standard: 1,024 starts from 153 trajectories; extended: 256 starts from four long trajectories.

Table is best read relative to screen replacement: scrolling replaces the entire visible screen in roughly 45 frames.

The decline from 32.83 dB at horizon 1 to 19.99 dB at 45 therefore marks a transition to fully generated geometry, not only compounding error.

Thereafter PSNR is nearly flat within the extended cohort (19.78/19.49/19.39 dB at horizons 45/100/200): long rollouts can remain coherent, but beyond one screen of travel they are not reliable counterfactual environments for PPO.

5

Figure instead isolates action sensitivity: from one fixed context, changing one action makes the jump branch clear the spike while idle collides.

Across all 22,745 development transitions, the factual action has lower next-frame negative log-likelihood than its flipped counterpart in 69.52% of contexts.

The trajectory-mean advantage is 0.165 nats per visual token (95% episode-bootstrap interval [0.150, 0.181]); factual-action token accuracy is 29.58% versus 27.78% after flipping, and 11.04% of argmax token predictions change.

2

: Figure 2Action-conditioning diagnostic from one shared four-frame context. The rows are aligned at $t+1$ and $t+5$ : changing only the first future action makes the idle branch collide and terminate, while the jump branch clears the spike and lands by $t+13$ .

: Table 6Matched dynamics-loss ablations on fixed development data. uses structured SLS and CPC; other row names denote the changed component. Action advantage is the episode-mean factual-versus-flipped NLL difference. Rollout columns average horizons 1/5/10/20/45. Each row is one run; bold is best.Ours

Table averages each rollout curve over the five horizons; Ours leads accuracy and PSNR while minimizing token-marginal JS, and removing CPC worsens every endpoint.

Removing SLS improves death F1 and factual-action advantage but reduces all three rollout aggregates, whereas uniform smoothing attains the highest death F1 but the weakest rollout profile.

These single-run diagnostics support CPC and associate FSQ-structured smoothing with better rollout fidelity, without establishing training variance or downstream policy effects.

6

Rollout horizon.

The roughly compute-matched seed-43 $H=20$ probe changes macro-average live survival by $+1.9\%$ relative to $H=45$ , with a 95% stratified-bootstrap interval of $[-8.1,13.5]\%$ ; every per-layout interval includes zero.

Thus 20-step dreams preserve observed performance and show that late $H=45$ states are not necessary for this run, but the single seed, unequal attempts, and co-varying iteration count preclude an isolated horizon claim.

6

DashVMC studies one deterministic binary-action game, with one post-freeze layout within known mechanics.

Repeated level prefixes make model diagnostics in-distribution; three controller seeds share one tokenizer and dynamics checkpoint, measuring controller rather than end-to-end uncertainty.

A matched seed-43 spatial-only probe finds no consistent live deficit after removing $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ , but its 10-attempt comparison does not establish equivalence; no direct frame-stack controller isolates the value of discrete visual tokens.

Death calibration covers only recorded states, leaving recursive reward exploitation unquantified.

Loss ablations are single-run model diagnostics; controller-input and $H=20$ probes are single-seed, and the latter is only roughly compute matched.

One-GPU access constrained multi-seed ablations and scaling curves, while wall-clock live evaluation limited deployment tests.

Finally, 60-FPS behavioural equivalence is probed on one checkpoint and layout, and reported speed depends on the RTX 2060 and compact edge representation.

7

DashVMC turns a fixed archive of roughly two hours of action-labelled gameplay into an interactive, action-conditioned predictive model of the game.

Its latent rollouts form a learned environment for offline model-based reinforcement learning: PPO improves BC-initialized controllers without additional live interaction, and the resulting policies consistently outlive their BC parents after zero-shot transfer to the non-paused game.

The deployed pipeline meets the game’s 60-Hz timing budget, while the spatial-only ablation shows that the learned dynamics can enable policy improvement without remaining in the live control path.

Under data scarcity, the world model thus acts as an interface between past experience and future decisions without prescribing how it must be used: DashVMC uses that interface for imagined policy optimization, while planning-based agents could instead query it at evaluation time.

Acknowledgments

We thank Clément Chatelain and Robin Condat for their guidance during the Representation Learning course at INSA Rouen Normandy, in which this project began, and CRIANN for providing the computing resources used for training.

We thank Maël Planchot for contributing gameplay data.

Geometry Dash is developed by RobTop Games.

一句话：只用约 2 小时录像学世界模型，在消费级 GPU 上维持 60Hz 的「截帧→预测→动作」闭环。

要点：

  • 从约 2 小时的 Geometry Dash 录像里学紧凑的动作条件世界模型，每个动作预测 64 token 的下一帧网格
  • 控制器先行为克隆，再完全在冻结模型的 rollout 里用 PPO 精修，不再与活游戏交互
  • 部署时跳过视觉生成，在消费级 GPU 上维持 60Hz 的采集到动作闭环；三个控制器种子在三个官图与一张社区图上都活得更久

为什么值得看：活游戏不能等策略——这篇把「不暂停、不降帧」作为硬约束，给出了世界模型在线控制的可行落地形态。

中文摘要：世界模型智能体通常在可以等策略的模拟器里评测，而活游戏施加的约束正相反：必须在下一帧到来前完成采集、预测与动作。DashVMC 从约两小时的 Geometry Dash 录像中学习一个紧凑的、以动作为条件的世界模型，每步预测 64 token 的下一帧离散网格。为了验证学到的动力学是否真的可用，控制器先用行为克隆初始化，再完全在冻结世界模型的 rollout 里用 PPO 精修，全程不再与活游戏交互。三个随机种子的精修策略在三个官方关卡与一张留出的社区布局上，存活时间都超过行为克隆初始版本。部署阶段它干脆跳过视觉生成，在消费级 GPU 上维持 60Hz 的采集到动作回路，说明即便长程保真度不完美，这种表示仍足以支撑控制。

主题：AI Native Engine

来源：arXiv·cs.LG（English）

License: CC BY 4.0

arXiv:2609.40003v1 [cs.LG] 30 Sep 2026\metadata

[Project page][Code]

tariolle.github.io/dash-vmc

\metadata

github.com/Tariolle/dash-vmc

\correspondence

DashVMC

Abstract

World-model agents are usually evaluated in simulators that can wait for the policy; live games impose the opposite constraint, requiring capture, prediction, and action before the next frame.

We present , which learns a compact, action-conditioned world model from approximately two hours of recorded Geometry Dash gameplay.

To test whether the learned dynamics are actionable, a controller is initialized by behavioural cloning (BC) and refined with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) entirely in frozen-model rollouts, without further interaction with the live game.

Across three controller seeds, the refined policies survive longer than their BC initializations on all three official levels and a held-out community layout.

At deployment, the baseline skips visual generation and sustains a 60-Hz capture-to-action loop on a consumer GPU.

Action-conditioned continuations and rollout diagnostics show that the model remains useful for control despite imperfect long-horizon fidelity.DashVMC

1

A world model learns transition dynamics $p_{\theta}(s_{t+1}\mid s_{t},a_{t})$ and can be rolled forward so that an agent practices without further environment interaction .

DashVMC asks whether such practice can improve a policy that must then act in a live, non-paused game.

It predicts a 64-token next grid in parallel for inexpensive imagined rollouts.

The baseline deployment skips generation and reuses the transformer’s temporal summary; a matched ablation tests whether the transformer must remain in the live loop.(; )

LeCun, 2022

Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018

Most world-model agents are evaluated in synchronous environments that wait for the policy.

A live, non-paused application reverses that contract: screen capture, perception, inference, and action dispatch must finish before the action becomes stale.

Geometry Dash is a small but unforgiving test of this contract.

The avatar moves continuously, the action space is binary, and a mistimed jump causes immediate death.

Levels are deterministic, but the agent observes only captured pixels and acts through keyboard events; it does not receive emulator state during control.

The apparent simplicity therefore isolates a demanding question: can an agent learn when to act from pixels, improve without touching the live game, and still react within narrow timing windows on modest hardware?

DashVMC follows the perception–dynamics–control organization of World Models : it compresses each frame into a discrete grid, learns action-conditioned grid dynamics, initializes a lightweight action model with BC, and refines it with PPO in the frozen model.()

Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018

()

Schulman et al., 2017

Our contributions are:

1.

a compact discrete, action-conditioned world model learned from approximately two hours of offline gameplay, whose rollouts support policy refinement without further live-game interaction;

2.

a decoder-free baseline that sustains a 60-Hz capture-to-action loop on a consumer GPU, together with a spatial-only variant that removes the transformer at inference without a consistent live-performance deficit; and

3.

evidence that the learned dynamics are actionable: controllers refined only in frozen-model rollouts improve over their exact BC parents on all three official levels across three seeds and on a held-out layout.

Diagnostics cover action sensitivity, rollout fidelity, controller input, dynamics losses, and latency.

2

World models and imagination.

World Models demonstrated that a compact controller optimized in learned dreams can transfer to the real environment .

IRIS combines a discrete autoencoder with an autoregressive transformer for data-efficient Atari learning ; $\Delta$ -IRIS reduces sequence cost with discrete delta tokens and continuous context tokens ; DIAMOND uses diffusion for imagination-trained control ; and DreamerV3 scales categorical recurrent latents across domains .

TWISTER adds action-conditioned CPC to transformer dynamics , which DashVMC adopts alongside parallel spatial prediction.

Earlier screenshot-based Geometry Dash control used DQN and imitation under a fabricated timestep ; here the game clock continues during capture and inference.()

Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018

()

Micheli et al., 2023

()

Micheli et al., 2024

()

Alonso et al., 2024

()

Hafner et al., 2025

()

Burchi and Timofte, 2025

()

Li and Rafferty, 2017

FSQ tokenization and policy initialization.

FSQ replaces learned vector-quantization codebooks with bounded scalar levels, avoiding commitment losses and codebook collapse while exposing an integer coordinate lattice ; we use the improved iFSQ bounding function .

Demonstration-based RL can reduce costly early exploration ; here recorded actions initialize the controller, while the retained policy is selected only after imagined PPO refinement.

Deterministic Sobel preprocessing removes appearance detail before tokenization, providing a compact task-specific alternative to richer continuous or generative representations.()

Mentzer et al., 2024

()

Lin et al., 2026

(; )

Hester et al., 2018

Baker et al., 2022

3

DashVMC is organized around a simple loop: recorded play trains a world model, the action model is refined in rollouts from the frozen dynamics model, and the resulting controller is returned to the live game.

The visual encoder, dynamics model, and action model are trained in sequence and then frozen for deployment.

Figure shows how the same learned state supports both imagined practice and live reaction.

1

: Figure 1Learning in imagination and acting in the live game. A recorded context seeds the frozen world model; the action model chooses what to do, the world model predicts the consequence, and PPO updates only the action model. In the baseline live path, the encoder and temporal context provide the state used for action selection, while visual generation is skipped.(a)(b)

3.1

Each RGB capture is cropped, converted to grayscale, filtered with Sobel edges, and resized to $64\times 64$ .

A convolutional autoencoder maps the result through three stride-2 stages to a four-channel $8\times 8$ latent map.

Each spatial vector is independently quantized with iFSQ levels $[8,5,5,5]$ , using the bounding function $2\operatorname{sigmoid}(1.6z)-1$ , and yields $64$ token IDs from $1000$ implicit codes .

The tokenizer is trained on adjacent frames with reconstruction, temporal-slowness, and latent-uniformity objectives .

Once selected, its encoder is frozen; its decoder is used to visualize dreams but is not required by the action model.(; )

Mentzer et al., 2024

Lin et al., 2026

()

Xia et al., 2025

3.2

The dynamics model is an eight-layer, width-384 transformer that receives four recent frame–action pairs.

Each frame block contains 64 visual tokens and one / status token, with action tokens inserted between blocks; a final masked block requests the next frame.

Attention is bidirectional within a frame and causal across frame/action blocks, so all next-frame positions are predicted in one forward pass without seeing their targets.

An explicit action token separates consecutive frames, so the model can answer the question central to policy learning: what changes if the action model jumps rather than idles?

It predicts all 64 codes of the next grid in parallel, together with an / score, and exposes a temporal summary $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ , taken from the most recent action-token position, to the action model.

Parallel prediction keeps imagined steps inexpensive.alivedeathalivedeath

Training combines next-grid prediction with action-conditional contrastive predictive coding of weight 0.1 , context corruption, and an auxiliary death objective.

For context corruption, 5% of context tokens are replaced uniformly and another 5% with adjacent FSQ codes.

The token loss uses focal modulation and structured label smoothing (SLS): for target lattice coordinate $\mathbf{c}_{i}$ , smoothing mass $\varepsilon=0.1$ is distributed over non-target codes proportionally to $\exp(-\|\mathbf{c}_{i}-\mathbf{c}_{j}\|_{2}^{2}/2\sigma^{2})$ , with $\sigma=0.9$ .

Focal modulation is applied once to the aggregate soft-target cross-entropy, and the output projection is tied to the token embedding.(; )

Burchi and Timofte, 2025

van den Oord et al., 2018

()

Lin et al., 2017

3.3

The $45{,}546$ -parameter actor–critic embeds the current token grid, processes it with two convolutions and max pooling, and concatenates the resulting 256-dimensional feature with the dynamics model’s temporal summary $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ .

Separate heads predict jump probability, value, and an eight-action auxiliary output covering the current and next seven actions.

The matched spatial-only ablation removes $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ from BC, PPO, and deployment, leaving a 41,706-parameter action model; the world model still generates its PPO rollouts.

BC first reproduces recorded action timing; PPO then departs from imitation through repeated imagined consequences.

Each PPO iteration generates 512 imagined episodes of at most 45 steps from recorded four-frame contexts, with greedy next-grid predictions and sampled Bernoulli actions.

The first four generated transitions refresh the context but are excluded because the recorded approach may make collision unavoidable; the remainder covers visible obstacles before invented geometry dominates.

Rollouts terminate when the death logit exceeds the logit; because death frames are oversampled $5\times$ , this is an operational boundary rather than a calibrated probability.

Reward is $+1$ per survived step and $-0.25$ per jump, discouraging a local optimum in which an early jump merely delays collision while airborne and earns extra survival reward without clearing the obstacle.

We use Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) with $\gamma=0.995$ , $\lambda=0.95$ , PPO clip 0.2, and auxiliary-action loss weight 0.1.alive()

Schulman et al., 2015

3.4

Training generates consequences; baseline live control only interprets recent observations.

Desktop Duplication captures only the $1032\times 1032$ model crop; CPU grayscale conversion followed by CUDA Sobel filtering and area resizing produces the $64\times 64$ observation.

Each frame is encoded and appended to a GPU-resident context, and the transformer runs context prefill only to produce $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ .

The live context marks every observation ; process-memory death detection only terminates and restarts an attempt outside the controller.

The next-grid predictor and image decoder are skipped, reducing the deployed path to 15.57 million parameters; the encoder uses , and transformer context encoding uses a CUDA Graph after warm-up.

The accelerated preprocessing path was checked against the recorded-data pipeline on synthetic and fresh live captures and produced byte-identical observations.

Spatial-only deployment loads only the frozen encoder and action model; both paths are reactive controllers whose policy improvement occurred during offline imagined training.alivetorch.compile

4

Data and training.

Before augmentation, the corpus contains 4,264 action-labelled gameplay episodes, or 251,963 frames and approximately 2.33 hours at the nominal 30-FPS capture cadence.

It includes deliberate failures, official Levels 1–7, several community levels, and 36 expert trajectories or segments totaling less than 20 minutes.

BC uses action labels from both the deliberate-failure and expert corpora.

Recording samples the current key state after each capture; deployment appends the new capture with the previously held state before dispatching the next, while process memory only segments deaths and restarts.

Mechanics outside the selected scope, including gravity inversion, are excluded.

Failure and expert trajectories are each split 90/10 with seed 42 at the base-episode level.

During tokenizer training, each adjacent-frame pair receives a shared two-dimensional translation whose horizontal and vertical offsets are sampled independently and uniformly from $[-4,4]$ pixels.

For dynamics training, the frozen encoder instead tokenizes each base episode at vertical offsets $\{-4,-2,0,2,4\}$ , expanding the corpus to 21,320 episode variants.

All windows and variants inherit their base-episode assignment; although no complete trajectories are duplicated, deterministic repeated attempts can share near-identical prefixes, so the 10% stratum is an in-distribution development set rather than a generalization test.

The tokenizer, dynamics model, and BC controller use this split; PPO draws rollout seeds from the full corpus and uses 512 fixed development contexts for checkpoint selection.

Tokenizer and dynamics training use seed 42, while controller training is repeated with seeds 43–45 under the same frozen representation and world model.

The first two stages run sequentially in BF16 on one A100, controller training runs in BF16 on one H200, and live inference and local latency evaluation use the same RTX 2060 with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu126 (CUDA 12.6).

: Table 1Training and checkpoint selection; tokenizer/dynamics learning rates use cosine decay.

The retained full runs took 3.19 A100 hours for the tokenizer, 4.20 A100 hours for the dynamics model, and 17.41 H200 hours for the seed-43 $H=45$ controller, including BC and 15,000 PPO iterations.

Thus the retained pipeline required 24.80 hours of sequential training while occupying one GPU at a time—roughly one day end to end.

The matched spatial-only controller took 17.12 H200 hours under the same iteration budget.

Checkpoint and live evaluation.

PPO checkpoint selection uses survival on 512 fixed latent development contexts every ten iterations.

All live checkpoints are then frozen and act deterministically from pixels alone; Auto-Retry standardizes restarts but provides no policy input.

For each seed, we compare PPO with the exact BC checkpoint that initialized it over 25 scored attempts on , , and .

BC and PPO attempts are separate samples paired only by lineage and run until detected death.

Background appearance cycles independently of level progress, while capture and dispatch phases vary near timing boundaries; repetitions measure this pixel-level deployment variability.

The protocol also covers , which begins at Level 1’s first ship section, and post-freeze community layout , a held-out test within supported mechanics.

To validate the earlier 30-FPS evaluations, a cadence check compares the identical frozen PPO checkpoint on Stereo Madness Copy over 25 optimized-path attempts at 60 FPS and 20 earlier diagnostic-path attempts at 30 FPS.Stereo MadnessBack on TrackPolargeistStereo Madness CopyStereo INSANE Nerfed

The endpoint is frames survived, except the cross-cadence probe uses wall time.

PPO-minus-BC intervals independently resample each frozen policy’s 25 attempts 50,000 times and characterize deployment variability; the three seed differences provide replication.

A post-freeze probe retrains seed 43 from the same BC parent with $H=20$ for 30,000 iterations (15.61 H200 hours), versus $H=45$ for 15,000 (17.41 hours), and scores 10 versus 25 attempts per layout.

Because horizon and iteration count co-vary, this is a roughly compute-matched shorter-rollout probe, not an isolated ablation.

A second seed-43 probe keeps the $H=45$ recipe and 15,000-iteration budget but removes $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ from controller training and inference.

It scores the resulting BC and PPO checkpoints over 10 attempts on the three official levels and held-out layout; comparisons with the 25-attempt temporal-state reference independently bootstrap the two frozen-policy samples.

Latency and continuation protocols.

Live latency covers capture through dispatch over 5,000 optimized-path frames.

The qualitative intervention starts immediately before a spike from one encoded four-frame prefix; greedy branches differ only in their first action and then idle.

Quantitative diagnostics re-encode the unaugmented development trajectories, yielding 22,745 next-frame windows from 413 usable trajectories.

The paired intervention flips only the final context action and bootstraps trajectories 5,000 times; autoregressive diagnostics greedily feed predictions back while replaying recorded actions.

The standard cohort has 1,024 starts from 153 trajectories; the exploratory 200-step cohort has 256 starts from the only four sufficiently long trajectories.

Targeted dynamics-loss ablations.

We compare the reported structured-SLS+CPC dynamics model with three single-training-run variants: uniform label smoothing with the same $\varepsilon=0.1$ , no label smoothing, and structured SLS without CPC.

They retain the tokenizer, corpus, split, architecture, seed 42, optimization, and maximum-development-death-F1 selection rule; all checkpoints share the exact evaluation windows and rollout starts.

External transition-latency protocol.

We also time the native imagined transition of DashVMC and released Pong checkpoints of IRIS and DIAMOND on the same RTX 2060.

Each runs in a fresh process at batch one with FP32 eager execution for 30 warm-ups and two repetitions of 100 synchronized transitions; differing native interfaces make this a cost, not quality, comparison.

5

5.1

The central question is whether policy improvement learned only through frozen-model rollouts transfers beyond imitation to the live game.

The selected tokenizer reconstructs development edge maps at 34.10 dB PSNR, and the dynamics model reaches 29.58% visual-token accuracy.

Deaths comprise 1.80% of its 22,745 development windows; at threshold 0.5 the death head obtains 0.721 precision, 0.883 recall, 0.794 F1, 0.994 AUROC, and 0.050 expected calibration error.

Because this stratum selected the dynamics checkpoint, these are in-distribution development diagnostics rather than untouched test results.

These component metrics establish a usable but imperfect imagined environment; the live comparison below tests whether it nevertheless teaches better actions.

: Table 2Live survival on all five layouts. No-op entries are mean frames $\pm$ standard deviation over 10 attempts and are shared across seeds. BC/PPO entries use 25 attempts; $\Delta$ is PPO minus its exact parent BC [95% attempt-level bootstrap interval]. The first three are official levels, Stereo Madness Copy begins in ship form, and Stereo INSANE Nerfed is held out.

LevelPolicySeed 43Seed 44Stereo MadnessNo-opshared: $46.2\pm 0.7$ BC $120.2\pm 91.8$ $130.6\pm 76.0$ PPO $\boldsymbol{280.1\pm 23.3}$ $\boldsymbol{280.4\pm 33.5}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $159.9\ [122.7,195.4]$ $149.8\ [116.8,180.6]$ Back on TrackNo-opshared: $63.4\pm 0.7$ BC $123.5\pm 81.5$ $111.1\pm 60.3$ PPO $\boldsymbol{260.0\pm 55.5}$ $\boldsymbol{195.9\pm 126.5}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $136.5\ [98.8,174.4]$ $84.8\ [31.9,139.6]$ PolargeistNo-opshared: $41.5\pm 0.7$ BC $52.4\pm 16.7$ $49.0\pm 16.5$ PPO $\boldsymbol{65.2\pm 33.4}$ $\boldsymbol{68.3\pm 44.1}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $12.8\ [-0.2,28.6]$ $19.4\ [3.0,39.0]$ Stereo Madness CopyNo-opshared: $135.0\pm 0.0$ BC $366.8\pm 172.8$ $285.7\pm 153.5$ PPO $\boldsymbol{435.6\pm 196.1}$ $\boldsymbol{495.8\pm 137.5}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $68.8\ [-33.3,166.1]$ $210.1\ [127.9,285.5]$ Stereo INSANE NerfedNo-opshared: $46.1\pm 0.8$ BC $104.8\pm 72.1$ $102.1\pm 64.0$ PPO $\boldsymbol{290.4\pm 48.6}$ $\boldsymbol{342.8\pm 80.8}$ $\Delta$ [95% CI] $185.5\ [151.1,217.6]$ $240.6\ [200.8,280.2]$

In Table , BC exceeds no-op everywhere and PPO improves over its parent in all fifteen seed-level comparisons.

Across the three controller seeds, the paired improvements are $154.2\pm 5.2$ frames on , $103.5\pm 28.7$ on , and $16.3\pm 3.3$ on , where the variation is the sample standard deviation across the three seed differences.

Every interval on the first two levels excludes zero; the smaller Polargeist gain is positive for all seeds, but seed 43’s interval marginally includes zero.

Polargeist’s smaller gain may reflect its yellow-orb mechanic, which requires a second, precisely timed jump input while airborne and is absent from the preceding levels.

2

Stereo MadnessBack on TrackPolargeist

On Stereo Madness Copy, seed 43’s interval includes zero but seeds 44–45 exclude it (mean gain $175.4\pm 94.2$ ); on held-out Stereo INSANE Nerfed, all exclude zero (mean gain $198.3\pm 37.6$ ).

The Copy is not held out, but exposes strong altitude control from Level 1’s first ship section.

The 60-FPS cadence probe on Stereo Madness Copy yields similar observed real-time survival: mean recorded episode wall time is 17.72 s at 60 FPS versus 17.79 s at 30 FPS, with a 95% bootstrap interval of $[-1.04,0.89]$  s for the mean difference (60 FPS minus 30 FPS).

This limited one-checkpoint, one-layout probe supports cadence transfer there, not equivalence across the primary cube levels.

Runtime temporal-state ablation.

The matched spatial-only controller gives up 1.11 frames on the fixed dream-selection metric, reaching 29.02/45 versus 30.13/45 for the seed-43 temporal-state reference.

: Table 3Seed-43 controller-input ablation (mean frames $\pm$ sample SD). Dream is best survival on the same 512 fixed contexts; live results use 25 attempts for the temporal-state reference and 10 for spatial-only.

Live performance is largely retained without $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ .

This suggests that temporal state contributes little in this predominantly reactive game, where the current grid exposes nearby geometry and avatar position and recent history mainly disambiguates motion such as scrolling and vertical velocity.

A memory-dependent environment would be expected to show a larger drop when $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ is removed.

Although $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ improves dream-selection survival by 1.11 frames, the world model’s demonstrated role remains to provide PPO’s offline training environment.

5.2

The complete perception-to-action loop must finish within 16.67 ms; at 60 Hz it can revise the binary key state every frame, not press 60 times per second.

While the RTX 2060 also renders the game, 5,000 measurements have mean/median 12.018/12.083 ms, p95 14.068 ms, p99 14.913 ms, and maximum 24.059 ms.

Eleven frames (0.22%) exceed the period; on a miss the loop skips its pacing sleep and immediately begins the next capture rather than reusing an old action.

This doubles the temporal resolution of the 30-FPS demonstrations.

Qualitatively, the ship policy uses sustained thrust and release intervals: ship motion remains correctable in flight, whereas a cube jump is largely ballistic until landing and therefore demands sparser, more precise timing.

The smooth, low-duty-cycle behaviour is consistent with PPO’s per-step jump penalty, although it does not isolate that penalty’s effect.

5.3

DashVMC’s native imagined transition averages 11.05 ms, compared with 49.30 ms for DIAMOND and 177.83 ms for IRIS, corresponding to 4.5 $\times$ and 16.1 $\times$ lower latency, respectively.

Only DashVMC fits the 16.67-ms 60-FPS period on this hardware.

: Table 4Batch-1 native imagined-transition latency on an RTX 2060 (synchronized run means in milliseconds). Interfaces differ, so this compares operational cost rather than quality.

Parallel grid prediction and latent-space feedback avoid autoregressive token generation and pixel decoding at every imagined step, compounding the savings through PPO.

5.4

Beyond its 45-step training horizon, the model feeds predicted grids and new actions back into context.

Interactive rollouts reproduce scrolling terrain, camera and height changes, collisions, and avatar transformations; long continuations may remain coherent or eventually repeat, empty, or invent impossible geometry.

Video demonstrations of interactive level continuations are available on the .

project page

: Table 5Recorded-action rollout diagnostics. Accuracy and decoder-space PSNR compare predicted with recorded grids; JS compares pooled token marginals. Standard: 1,024 starts from 153 trajectories; extended: 256 starts from four long trajectories.

Table is best read relative to screen replacement: scrolling replaces the entire visible screen in roughly 45 frames.

The decline from 32.83 dB at horizon 1 to 19.99 dB at 45 therefore marks a transition to fully generated geometry, not only compounding error.

Thereafter PSNR is nearly flat within the extended cohort (19.78/19.49/19.39 dB at horizons 45/100/200): long rollouts can remain coherent, but beyond one screen of travel they are not reliable counterfactual environments for PPO.

5

Figure instead isolates action sensitivity: from one fixed context, changing one action makes the jump branch clear the spike while idle collides.

Across all 22,745 development transitions, the factual action has lower next-frame negative log-likelihood than its flipped counterpart in 69.52% of contexts.

The trajectory-mean advantage is 0.165 nats per visual token (95% episode-bootstrap interval [0.150, 0.181]); factual-action token accuracy is 29.58% versus 27.78% after flipping, and 11.04% of argmax token predictions change.

2

: Figure 2Action-conditioning diagnostic from one shared four-frame context. The rows are aligned at $t+1$ and $t+5$ : changing only the first future action makes the idle branch collide and terminate, while the jump branch clears the spike and lands by $t+13$ .

: Table 6Matched dynamics-loss ablations on fixed development data. uses structured SLS and CPC; other row names denote the changed component. Action advantage is the episode-mean factual-versus-flipped NLL difference. Rollout columns average horizons 1/5/10/20/45. Each row is one run; bold is best.Ours

Table averages each rollout curve over the five horizons; Ours leads accuracy and PSNR while minimizing token-marginal JS, and removing CPC worsens every endpoint.

Removing SLS improves death F1 and factual-action advantage but reduces all three rollout aggregates, whereas uniform smoothing attains the highest death F1 but the weakest rollout profile.

These single-run diagnostics support CPC and associate FSQ-structured smoothing with better rollout fidelity, without establishing training variance or downstream policy effects.

6

Rollout horizon.

The roughly compute-matched seed-43 $H=20$ probe changes macro-average live survival by $+1.9\%$ relative to $H=45$ , with a 95% stratified-bootstrap interval of $[-8.1,13.5]\%$ ; every per-layout interval includes zero.

Thus 20-step dreams preserve observed performance and show that late $H=45$ states are not necessary for this run, but the single seed, unequal attempts, and co-varying iteration count preclude an isolated horizon claim.

6

DashVMC studies one deterministic binary-action game, with one post-freeze layout within known mechanics.

Repeated level prefixes make model diagnostics in-distribution; three controller seeds share one tokenizer and dynamics checkpoint, measuring controller rather than end-to-end uncertainty.

A matched seed-43 spatial-only probe finds no consistent live deficit after removing $\mathbf{h}_{t}$ , but its 10-attempt comparison does not establish equivalence; no direct frame-stack controller isolates the value of discrete visual tokens.

Death calibration covers only recorded states, leaving recursive reward exploitation unquantified.

Loss ablations are single-run model diagnostics; controller-input and $H=20$ probes are single-seed, and the latter is only roughly compute matched.

One-GPU access constrained multi-seed ablations and scaling curves, while wall-clock live evaluation limited deployment tests.

Finally, 60-FPS behavioural equivalence is probed on one checkpoint and layout, and reported speed depends on the RTX 2060 and compact edge representation.

7

DashVMC turns a fixed archive of roughly two hours of action-labelled gameplay into an interactive, action-conditioned predictive model of the game.

Its latent rollouts form a learned environment for offline model-based reinforcement learning: PPO improves BC-initialized controllers without additional live interaction, and the resulting policies consistently outlive their BC parents after zero-shot transfer to the non-paused game.

The deployed pipeline meets the game’s 60-Hz timing budget, while the spatial-only ablation shows that the learned dynamics can enable policy improvement without remaining in the live control path.

Under data scarcity, the world model thus acts as an interface between past experience and future decisions without prescribing how it must be used: DashVMC uses that interface for imagined policy optimization, while planning-based agents could instead query it at evaluation time.

Acknowledgments

We thank Clément Chatelain and Robin Condat for their guidance during the Representation Learning course at INSA Rouen Normandy, in which this project began, and CRIANN for providing the computing resources used for training.

We thank Maël Planchot for contributing gameplay data.

Geometry Dash is developed by RobTop Games.

item.title: 让 AI 智能体能改引擎：确定性模拟、命令模式与文本化验证 ｜ 搭建游戏AI适配框架：确定性模拟、命令模式与文本化验证
item.description:
一句话：想让 Agent 参与引擎开发，先还架构债：确定性、扁平对象、可回放命令流。

要点：

  • 启动阶段固定单一随机种子，玩法判定统一走受控随机源，保证任意时刻状态可精确复现
  • 把状态变更抽象成可序列化命令，用文本指令驱动游戏实例回放，调数值不必重新编译引擎
  • 验证环节不用全屏截图，改用 odiff 做命令行图像差分输出量化重合百分比，用 samply 把性能瓶颈转成纯文本调用栈

为什么值得看：Agent 改不动游戏不是模型不够强，而是引擎不可复现、不可无头运行；这四条改造顺序值得照抄。

中文摘要：通用代码助手在常规软件上表现稳定，但进到传统游戏开发常出现断层：物理表现、状态流转与渲染逻辑无法只靠静态源码呈现，调用大模型往往停留在通用代码修补、无法闭环验证。文章给出四条改造路径：一是用单一随机种子与受控随机源建立确定性状态；二是把多继承的面向对象结构压成单一对象模型（如统一的 Thing 结构体），便于序列化与提示词理解；三是把状态变更抽象为命令对象，用文本指令直接回放，避免每次调参都重新编译；四是把纯逻辑内核剥离成独立库，让引擎退化成只负责呈现的哑终端。验证层面主张文本化：图像差分用 odiff 输出量化百分比，性能剖析用 samply 输出调用栈文本，避免高分辨率截图污染上下文。作者也提醒：超休闲小游戏强上这套会拖慢进度，卡牌构筑、长线策略这类规则复杂的项目收益最大。

主题：AI Native Engine

来源：公众号·007游戏Agent（中文）

通用代码辅助工具在处理常规软件时表现稳定，但在传统游戏开发中常面临断层。传统游戏包含大量非代码构件，运行时的物理表现、状态流转和渲染逻辑无法仅通过静态源码完全呈现。当开发管线过度依赖不可见的游戏黑盒时，调用大语言模型往往只停留在通用代码修补，无法闭环验证逻辑改动。

让自动化工具介入深度开发的核心，在于为项目搭建专属测试载体。通用辅助工具能够处理文本和函数编写，但理解游戏需要运行状态层面的读写能力。使智能体能够在开发循环中自主修改并验证，前提是将游戏状态重构成高度透明、可量化的确定性系统。

确定性状态与扁平对象

状态难以复现是游戏自动化调试的主要障碍。常规开发中零散调用的伪随机逻辑会导致每次运行路径不一致。解决方式是在工程启动阶段确立单一随机数种子，所有涉及玩法判定的逻辑统一调用受控随机源，确保在相同输入下能够精确重现任意时刻的状态。

多层继承的面向对象结构会占用过量提示词空间，增加模型理解调用关系的负担。采用单一对象模型（例如统一的 Thing 结构体）能够改善这一情况。游戏内的树木、单位或装备均由带有枚举类型和数值字段的基础结构体构成，逻辑根据类型字段执行相应分支。这种结构减少了类关系推理的歧义，同时统一了序列化与反序列化接口，使整个关卡状态能够直接转为列表进行快速存取。

命令解耦与独立模拟

自动化迭代的效率受制于等待时间。如果每次调整基础数值或移动逻辑都需要重新编译引擎，智能体执行调优的循环周期会被拉长。将状态变更抽象为命令模式，把玩家交互和系统动作打包成可序列化的结构对象，能够实现用文本指令直接驱动游戏实例回放，无需反复启动图形客户端。

静态运行数据同样需要与逻辑实现拆离。把移动速度、攻击伤害等固定配置剥离到外部文本或数据表格，在运行时直接反序列化注入实体对象。团队成员与自动化工具均可在脱离引擎编辑器的前提下直接修改构建版本，省去重复打包耗时。

更彻底的解耦是建立独立模拟内核。如《Monster Train》和《Solium Infernum》所采用的黑盒架构，玩法规则被封装进独立的动态链接库，游戏引擎仅充当接收状态差分并负责呈现的哑终端。纯 C# 逻辑层脱离场景渲染、音效和模型加载单独运行，让自动化测试能够在控制台环境下以极高频率批处理逻辑检验。

文本化验证与适用边界

当智能体完成修改后，需要明确的反馈机制判断结果偏差。直接向多模态模型输入高分辨率全屏截图会引入冗余视觉噪点，形成上下文污染。引入命令行图像差分工具 odiff，能够提取裁剪区域的差异图并输出量化重合百分比，为智能体提供稳定的数值收敛目标。

性能分析同样需要规避依赖人眼观察的图形化界面。集成纯文本分析工具 samply，将性能瓶颈转为控制台日志流输出，使智能体能够根据调用栈文本直接定位开销过大的函数分支，完成修改与验证的闭环循环。

构建这类状态隔离系统的代价在于前期架构重构的高昂成本。例如在几周即可交付的超休闲单屏小游戏中，强行剥离模拟库和单一对象不仅无法提升效率，反而会让初期代码量成倍增加；但对于规则交错的卡牌构筑或长线策略游戏，若不剥离逻辑内核，每次验证卡牌联动都需要启动完整场景等待数十秒，而无头仿真环境下仅需几十毫秒即可跑完数百回合判定。自建游戏载体的收益取决于逻辑复杂度与长期自动化测试的调用频次。

内容配图关于蒸蒸实时自动抓取游戏新闻并摘要，人类小编从游戏设计和投研角度提问，Agent 蒸蒸会启动 agent loop 做调研并给出结果，每日精选问题和回答。

欢迎大家提供自己感兴趣的新闻或者问题，我们会转给蒸蒸。

性能分析同样需要规避依赖人眼观察的图形化界面。集成纯文本分析工具 samply，将性能瓶颈转为控制台日志流输出，使智能体能够根据调用栈文本直接定位开销过大的函数分支，完成修改与验证的闭环循环。

构建这类状态隔离系统的代价在于前期架构重构的高昂成本。例如在几周即可交付的超休闲单屏小游戏中，强行剥离模拟库和单一对象不仅无法提升效率，反而会让初期代码量成倍增加；但对于规则交错的卡牌构筑或长线策略游戏，若不剥离逻辑内核，每次验证卡牌联动都需要启动完整场景等待数十秒，而无头仿真环境下仅需几十毫秒即可跑完数百回合判定。自建游戏载体的收益取决于逻辑复杂度与长期自动化测试的调用频次。

内容配图关于蒸蒸实时自动抓取游戏新闻并摘要，人类小编从游戏设计和投研角度提问，Agent 蒸蒸会启动 agent loop 做调研并给出结果，每日精选问题和回答。

欢迎大家提供自己感兴趣的新闻或者问题，我们会转给蒸蒸。

item.title: 面向高光的光照缓存：反射方向参数化 + 粗糙度相关的预滤波辐射 ｜ Neural Caching of Prefiltered Radiance for Specular Lighting
item.description:
一句话：把神经辐射缓存的输入换成反射方向、目标换成预滤波辐射，再与 BRDF 积分图配合。

要点：

  • 网络预测的是每个表面点的预滤波入射辐射，而不是直接回归出射辐射，天然带粗糙度语义
  • 输入使用反射方向参数化，输出与预计算的 BRDF 积分图通过 split-sum 近似合成出射辐射
  • 在线训练、渲染时持续更新缓存；在 Bunny 与 Specular Sponza 上比对照的 NRC 基线更快收敛到路径追踪参考，高光质量更好

为什么值得看：实时路径追踪里高光是最慢收敛的一项，这套「预滤波 + split-sum」的组合可以直接接到现有 NRC 管线上。

中文摘要：神经辐射缓存（NRC）为实时路径追踪提供场景光照的在线神经表示，但它对高光反射的拟合一直不理想。本文给出一个面向高光定制的 NRC 变体：输入改用反射方向参数化，监督目标改成与粗糙度相关的预滤波辐射，网络只预测每个表面点上预滤波后的入射辐射，再与预先算好的 BRDF 积分图通过 split-sum 近似组合，得到出射辐射。这样的分解让网络不必同时学材质响应与方向积分。方法全程在线训练，渲染过程中持续调整自己的缓存。在 Bunny 与 Specular Sponza 上，报告的结果显示它相对所评测的 NRC 基线收敛到累积路径追踪参考更快、高光质量更好，同时保持实时性能。

主题：AI Rendering

来源：arXiv·cs.GR（English）

Neural Caching of Prefiltered Radiance for Specular Lighting

42Volume: 3Issue: D.  Klepikov, V.  FrolovLomonosow Moscow State University

Abstract

Neural Radiance Caching (NRC)  provides an online neural representation of scene illumination for real-time path tracing. This paper presents an NRC variant tailored to specular lighting through a reflection-direction parameterization and a roughness-dependent radiance target. Our network predicts prefiltered incoming radiance at individual surface points, which is combined with a precomputed BRDF integration map using the split-sum approximation to estimate outgoing radiance. On Bunny and Specular Sponza, the reported comparisons indicate faster convergence to the accumulated path-tracing reference and improved specular-lighting quality relative to the evaluated NRC baselines. Our online-trained method maintains real-time performance while adapting its cache during rendering.[]

17

Computing methodologies Ray tracing

ccs

Computing methodologies Neural networks

ccs

†2023†year: †2023†year: †D. Archambault, R. Bujack, and T. Schreck†editors: †Eurographics Conference on Visualization CGF Vol No †subject: ††teaser:

Qualitative comparison on Bunny (first row) and Specular Sponza (second row), a version of Sponza with highly reflective, untextured surfaces. All renderings use only specular lobes. In Bunny, the walls and floor have roughness 0.1. The NRC baseline uses the implementation provided in . The reference is obtained by accumulating the Falcor path tracer over 4000 frames.[]

17

1

Specular reflection depends strongly on viewing direction and surface roughness, making its representation challenging for radiance caching. Neural Radiance Caching (NRC)  learns scene illumination online to accelerate path tracing. We target specular lighting by parameterizing the cache with the reflected viewing direction and learning roughness-dependent prefiltered incoming radiance for split-sum reconstruction.[]

17

The main goal of path-tracing is to calculate the solution of Light Transport Equation (LTE) :[]

10

$L_{o}(\omega_{o})=L_{e}(\omega_{o})+\int_{H^{+}}L_{i}(\omega_{i})f_{s}(\omega_{i},\omega_{o})\cos(\theta_{i})\,d\omega_{i}.$ (1)

Here, $L_{e}$ is the radiance emitted in direction $\omega_{o}$ , $L_{i}$ is the radiance arriving from direction $\omega_{i}$ , and $f_{s}$ is the bidirectional scattering distribution function (BSDF). The angle $\theta_{i}$ is measured between the surface normal $n$ at position $x$ and $\omega_{i}$ . We omit the position argument for brevity. For reflection, the BSDF is restricted to a bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF). In this work, we consider its specular component. Estimating the integral is computationally expensive, motivating approaches that cache previously computed lighting information.

Traditional radiance caching approaches like (and analogues) are based on several heuristics that are difficult to implement and tend to produce artefacts that need special care to be suppressed . Other progressive rendering and reconstruction approaches (for example ) also uses handcrafted mathematic models which makes their implementation and testing inside and existing rendering system a challenging task. At the same time NRC reduces such complexity by way of abstraction of internal radiance cache representation via neural network. This method represents scene illumination with a multilayer perceptron that maps hit ray positions and directions to radiance values of the scattered light. The approach is lightweight and it is designed to continuously train in real-time to support dynamic scenes while ensuring predictable performance and resource usage. The research presents a multitude of methods to regulate and stabilize the output of the neural network like self-training and path termination that are omitted in our paper. The idea of encoding input data was also explored in these papers .[]

12

[]

20

[]

14

[]

17

[]

15

[]

22

[]

16

Our method parameterizes the cache to represent specular reflection, including mirror-like and rough glossy reflection. Following the reflection-direction parameterization used in , we use the viewing direction reflected about the surface normal as a network input. We also use the split-sum approximation  to separate prefiltered lighting from the final BRDF reconstruction. The cache predicts roughness-dependent filtered radiance, while the BRDF integration lookup supplies the final Fresnel-dependent reconstruction. Together, these terms approximate the reflected component of Equation ().[]

22

[]

11

1

FLIP, SSIM, and MSE during online training on Bunny (first row) and Specular Sponza (second row). The horizontal axis measures rendering frames. Lower FLIP and MSE values and higher SSIM values indicate better agreement with the reference. MSE is displayed on a logarithmic scale. The curves compare our method with the evaluated NRC variants. Figure 1:

2

2.1

Microfacet theory is a popular approach to modelling surface reflection and transmission. In this theory, surfaces are modelled as a collection of small microfacets, with their aggregated statistical behaviour determining the observed scattering of light. The microfacet specular BRDF is an expression that describes the scattering of light from a surface composed of microfacets. To compute BRDF from such a model, local lighting effects at the microfacet level need to be considered, such as microfacet occlusion, shadowing, and interreflection. An expression representing BRDF consists of two statistical measures, a microfacet normalized distribution function(NDF) of facets represented as $D$ and a shadowing-masking function between facets $G$ , and a Fresnel reflectance factor $F$ . All of that is combined in a general Cook-Torrance microfacet specular shading model. Here $h$ is the halfway-vector between $\omega_{i},\omega_{o}$ .[]

8

[]

7

$f_{r}(\omega_{i},\omega_{o})=\frac{D(h)F(\omega_{o},h)G(\omega_{i},\omega_{o})}{4(n\cdot\omega_{i})(n\cdot\omega_{o})}$ (2)

For the implementation of those terms, we used ones implemented in the Falcor rendering framework and thoroughly described in Disney’s research paper . In the presented paper NDF is represented as a modified Trowbridge-Reitz(GGX) distribution. For the Fresnel term the Schlick approximation is used. For the shadowing-masking function modified GGX model is used with reparametrization presented in Disney’s research paper to dampen the shine on small roughness values.[]

4

[]

5

[]

21

[]

19

[]

23

2.2

The reflected component of Equation () can be estimated by importance sampling. Let $p(\omega_{i})$ denote the probability density of the sampled incoming direction, measured with respect to solid angle. We use the NDF-based sampling implementation provided by Falcor. For $N$ samples $\omega_{i,k}$ , the estimator is

1

$L_{o}(\omega_{o})=L_{e}(\omega_{o})+\int_{H^{+}}L_{i}(\omega_{i})f_{r}(\omega_{i},\omega_{o})\cos(\theta_{i})\,d\omega_{i}\\

\approx L_{e}(\omega_{o})+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{L_{i}(\omega_{i,k})f_{r}(\omega_{i,k},\omega_{o})\cos(\theta_{i,k})}{p(\omega_{i,k})}.$ (3)

Even with importance sampling, many samples may be required for high-quality results. Karis  approximates the reflected-radiance estimate by separating it into two averages:[]

11

$L_{o}(\omega_{o})-L_{e}(\omega_{o})\\

\approx\left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}L_{i}(\omega_{i,k})\right)\left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{f_{r}(\omega_{i,k},\omega_{o})\cos(\theta_{i,k})}{p(\omega_{i,k})}\right).$ (4)

The first factor represents prefiltered environment radiance. The practical prefilter in  samples the GGX normal distribution and uses normalized cosine weighting. During prefiltering, the viewing direction is assumed perpendicular to the filtering surface, so $n=\omega_{o}$ . The filtering normal is aligned with the reflected viewing direction used for lookup. Incoming directions $\omega_{i}$ remain sampled over the hemisphere. This normal-view assumption introduces approximation error at grazing viewing angles.[]

11

The second factor is the BRDF integration map. With Schlick’s Fresnel approximation, it is represented by two coefficients stored in a lookup texture indexed by roughness and the cosine of the viewing angle. Our method uses this split-sum factorization and BRDF integration lookup to reconstruct outgoing radiance from the neural cache.

2.3

We examined various methods employing neural networks (and multilayer perceptron specifically) for providing scene information. Neural methods are increasingly being used for rendering in various applications. The recent method of spatio-directional neural representations replaces traditional discrete representations with an MLP for reconstructing 3D geometry-aware solutions. The most widely adopted strategy currently is Neural Radiance Fields, the science publication of which inspired a multitude of works in the novel view synthesis problem.[]

13

[]

3

[]

22

Gradually, the interest in neural approaches for global illumination increased. There has been a significant effort to improve sampling and denoising of Monte Carlo global illumination algorithms . The current work is based on NRC where researchers use small neural networks that undergo online training to store and predict indirect global illumination for real-time path tracing. Further development shows the significant advantage of using hash grid parametric encoding for NRC.[]

16

[]

2

[]

6

[]

9

[]

17

[]

15

3

Our method uses a single multilayer perceptron to predict prefiltered incoming radiance at a queried position, reflection direction, and roughness. The network is trained during rendering to adapt to scene changes. We divide rendering into three passes. The first generates training paths with multiple surface bounces. The second traces rendering paths and stores the surface information needed to query the cache, terminating paths earlier than the training pass. Both passes use Monte Carlo integration and importance sampling for continuation directions. The third queries the cache and reconstructs outgoing radiance using the BRDF integration lookup.

For each surface hit, we collect the radiance and path-throughput information along the continuation of the training path. These data are used to reconstruct an RGB incoming-radiance target $Y$ , which is stored in the training buffer together with its cache query. Different sampled paths can produce different targets for the same query.

The cache query is $q=(\phi(x),\omega_{\mathrm{refl}},\rho)$ , where $x$ is the surface position, $\phi$ is its hash-grid encoding, and $\rho$ is the surface roughness. For an outgoing direction $\omega_{o}$ pointing away from the surface, the reflected direction is $\omega_{\mathrm{refl}}=2(n\cdot\omega_{o})n-\omega_{o}$ . We hash-grid encode positions  and pass reflection direction and roughness directly to the MLP. Each query produces an RGB estimate of the filtered incoming radiance. The roughness input conditions the cached lighting on the reflection lobe.[]

15

We train the network using mean squared error (MSE). Under squared-error loss, the population-optimal predictor is the conditional mean of the training target given the cache query,

$\widehat{L}^{\,*}(q)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid q].$ (5)

The sampling distribution and target weighting therefore determine the radiance filter represented by the cache. The network and optimization configuration follow . To reduce fluctuations during online adaptation, we use an exponential moving average of the optimized network weights. The final pass combines the predicted radiance with the stored BRDF integration map to estimate outgoing specular radiance in the camera direction. This reconstruction retains the split-sum approximation and its grazing-angle limitations.[]

17

4

We use the ray-tracing pipeline in Falcor  and the MLP implementation in tiny-cuda-nn . All images were rendered at a resolution of $1920\times 1080$ on an Intel Core i7-8700K processor with an NVIDIA RTX 3080 Ti graphics card. We evaluate image quality using FLIP , SSIM , and MSE on each rendering frame. MSE is displayed on a logarithmic scale because its values span a wide range. The reference image is obtained by accumulating the regular path tracer over 4000 frames.[]

4

[]

18

[]

1

[]

24

Our findings indicate that the modifications have not resulted in any discernible performance degradation while improving convergence and output quality. The BRDF integration map is precomputed and queried during rendering. The changes to the neural network inputs do not negatively influence the other major NRC components.

We compare our method with the NRC baseline and an NRC variant trained only on initial hits. We include the initial-hit variant because removing training targets from multiple hits along a path reduced NRC output quality in our tests. The two variants are distinguished in the comparison plots.

Figure  presents a qualitative comparison after 1000 rendering frames. The displayed images were adjusted for improved visibility. The FLIP results indicate closer agreement with the accumulated reference for our method than for the evaluated NRC baselines. Figure  shows the evolution of the quality metrics during training and indicates faster convergence for our method. On Bunny, our method achieves better image quality than the NRC baseline after 1000 frames.

1

5

We presented an NRC variant for real-time specular-lighting approximation that predicts roughness-dependent prefiltered incoming radiance and reconstructs outgoing radiance using the split-sum approximation. On Bunny and Specular Sponza, the reported comparisons show faster convergence and improved output quality relative to the evaluated NRC baselines while maintaining the same level of performance. The evaluated method uses hash-grid position encoding, a reflection-direction input, and split-sum reconstruction. It retains the grazing-angle limitations of the split-sum approximation. Online training enables the cache to adapt during rendering, motivating further investigation of its behavior in dynamic scenes.
