TexF’s spatial structure also offers representational versatility.

It naturally shares a voxel grid with grid-based implicit geometry,

such as an SDF, for joint geometry–appearance modeling.

Its attributes can also be sampled at mesh vertices for vertex-color rendering.

2 III-A

To support conventional UV-textured assets, we initialize TexF by sampling the mesh surface and transferring attributes from the source texture.

For each surface sample, its barycentric coordinates determine both its 3D position and UV coordinate. The UV coordinate is used to sample the source material maps, while the 3D position assigns the retrieved attributes to the corresponding voxel. Attributes assigned to the same voxel are averaged.

Conversely, TexF can be baked into a UV texture by rasterizing a target UV layout and querying the field at the corresponding surface positions, enabling compatibility with standard UV rendering pipelines.

Voxel discretization and interpolation introduce transfer errors, which we reduce through rendering-driven refinement in Sec. .

III-B

III-BTexF Rendering and Refinement

1 III-B

TexF rendering first rasterizes the mesh to determine visible surface positions, then queries the field at these positions to obtain texture attributes.

As illustrated in Fig. , UV rendering samples a 2D texture through interpolated UV coordinates, whereas TexF queries the field directly at $\mathbf{p}$ .

For the voxel representation defined in Eq. (), the color $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{p})$ is obtained by trilinearly interpolating neighboring texture attributes:

4

1

$\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{p})=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{p})}\omega_{i}\mathbf{t}(\mathbf{q}_{i}),\vskip-4.26773pt$ (2)

where $\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{p})$ denotes the set of active grid points within the $2\times 2\times 2$ neighborhood of $\mathbf{p}$ , and the trilinear weights $\omega_{i}$ are determined by the query position within the grid cell. This interpolation is mathematically analogous to bilinear sampling in UV rendering, but operates in 3D with weights renormalized over the available voxels.

In the rare case that no active corner is available, the nearest active voxel is used as a fallback.

We implement this rendering path using differentiable rasterization  and sparse-grid interpolation operators .

The interpolation in Eq. () is differentiable and can be evaluated in parallel, supporting real-time rendering and efficient backpropagation to the voxel attributes.

GPU-resident TexF uses the same rasterization stage, but interpolates latent features and decodes them with an MLP to obtain texture attributes (Sec. ).[]

48

[]

49

2

III-D

2 III-B

We use our differentiable renderer to refine texture appearance through inverse rendering. We render reference images $\{\mathbf{I}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}$ from the original lossless UV-textured mesh and corresponding images $\{\widehat{\mathbf{I}}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}$ from the target mesh with TexF under the same views. We minimize the photometric objective

$\mathcal{D}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left[\left\|\widehat{\mathbf{I}}_{i}-\mathbf{I}_{i}\right\|_{1}+1-\mathrm{SSIM}(\widehat{\mathbf{I}}_{i},\mathbf{I}_{i})\right],\vskip-2.84544pt$ (3)

where the $\ell_{1}$ term measures pixel-wise color errors and the SSIM term encourages structural similarity.

Starting from the transferred attributes, we optimize $\mathbf{t}(\mathbf{q})$ while keeping the mesh geometry and voxel support fixed.

Image-space supervision accounts for the sampling and interpolation used during rendering, allowing refinement to compensate for errors left by direct texture transfer and voxel discretization. It therefore improves the texture representation without increasing its capacity.

This refinement is also efficient, requiring only a modest optimization cost in our experiments.

The same objective also optimizes the latent features and decoder parameters of the compressed neural field (Sec. ).

III-D

Beyond compression refinement, the differentiable renderer could support mesh texturing directly from multi-view images. Extending it to jointly optimize geometry and appearance is another direction for future work.

III-CTexF Bitstream Compression

For disk storage and transmission, we seek a compact entropy-coded texture bitstream . TexF derives voxel locations from the mesh rather than encoding them separately.

As illustrated in Fig. , mesh geometry is encoded using an existing mesh codec .

The encoder and decoder apply the same voxelization procedure to the reconstructed mesh to obtain the voxel set $\mathbf{Q}$ .

These shared locations establish the correspondence between decoded attributes and TexF voxels, allowing the texture stream to carry coded attributes without per-voxel coordinates.[, ]

Their transform, prediction, and entropy-coding tools can therefore exploit spatial correlations directly in mesh-derived voxel neighborhoods, without requiring a texture-specific codec architecture.[]

III-DGPU-Resident TexF Compression

GPU-resident compression aims to reduce texture memory while supporting low-latency random access during rendering .

Although TexF is spatially sparse, its explicit attributes and lookup structure can still occupy substantial GPU memory at high resolutions. For example, our uncompressed implementation stores three 8-bit RGB values and a 64-bit lookup key per voxel.

We therefore develop 3D Neural Texture Compression (), which exploits TexF’s 3D-native organization to compress surface appearance into quantized features and a lightweight decoder.

Unlike NTC , which decodes texture attributes in the 2D UV domain, 3DNTC reconstructs them directly at continuous mesh surface positions, without UV mapping or explicit per-voxel lookup entries.[]

12

3DNTC[]

12

1 III-D

3DNTC uses two spatially downsampled hash grids with INT4 features to capture texture variations at different spatial scales, together with a shared four-layer FP16 MLP (Fig. ).

At level $i\in\{1,2\}$ , the grid resolution is $\lceil K/s_{i}\rceil$ , where $K$ is the reference spatial resolution set according to the source texture resolution, and $s_{i}$ is the downsampling factor (e.g., 4 or 8).

Following multiresolution hash encoding , each level uses a table of $2^{h_{i}}$ entries with $F$ feature channels, indexed by hashing integer grid coordinates.

These entries store shared latent features, without explicit per-voxel lookup keys.

Thus, the downsampling factor $s_{i}$ controls spatial granularity, while $h_{i}$ and $F$ determine latent storage; varying these parameters adjusts the rate–distortion trade-off.

6

[]

29

2 III-D

Rasterization provides visible surface positions as in Sec. .

For each position $\mathbf{p}$ , we hash the eight surrounding grid-corner coordinates at each level and trilinearly interpolate their features.

The interpolated features are concatenated across levels into $\Phi(\mathbf{p})\in\mathbb{R}^{2F}$ and combined with an 18-dimensional positional encoding $\gamma(\mathbf{p})$ .

A single evaluation of the decoder $D_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ then reconstructs color:

III-B

$\widehat{\mathbf{t}}(\mathbf{p})=D_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\!\left(\Phi(\mathbf{p}),\gamma(\mathbf{p})\right),$ (4)

Interpolating features before decoding yields the attribute directly at $\mathbf{p}$ , avoiding separate neural decoding of the eight voxel-corner colors.

The decoder has three hidden layers with 64, 48, and 32 channels and hardGELU activations, followed by a linear output layer;

its parameters are shared across all surface queries within each asset.

Only the packed latent tables and decoder parameters need to remain resident as texture data.

Queries are independent and require no sequential entropy decoding, enabling on-demand reconstruction during rendering.

3 III-D

For each asset, we sample continuous surface positions and obtain target attributes from the refined explicit TexF.

We jointly optimize the latent tables and MLP to minimize attribute mean squared error, simulating INT4 quantization during training.

We then refine both against ground-truth multi-view renderings using Eq. (), improving rendered fidelity without increasing the payload.

At deployment, only the packed latent tables and decoder parameters are needed as GPU-resident texture data.

In this section, we first present the common experimental settings and assess TexF’s representation fidelity, compactness, and rendering efficiency. Because the representation is the basis for subsequent compression, we first assess the fidelity and compactness of TexF, together with its construction and rendering efficiency.

We compare TexF with UV-reparameterized textures (UV-Reparam) generated using UVAtlas , a tool commonly used in mesh compression  to improve spatial continuity and coding efficiency through chart reparameterization and packing.

Direct UV-to-TexF texture transfer provides a strong initialization. Inverse rendering (IR) further compensates for transfer errors, improving fidelity without increasing representation capacity.

By default, we perform 30 optimization iterations, each using a batch of eight newly sampled perspective views, totaling 240 random views at a rendering resolution of $1024\times 1024$ .

Cameras look at the object center with a $45^{\circ}$ FOV. Azimuth, sine elevation, and distance are drawn from uniform distributions over $[0,2\pi)$ , $[-1,1]$ , and $[1.2,3.0]$ , respectively.

These training views are separate from the 16 fixed orthographic Fibonacci evaluation views mentioned above and differ in both viewing direction and projection.Inverse Rendering Refinement.

As shown in Fig. , IR improves PSNR and 3D-PSNR by 1.4 and 1.2 dB on average, alongside higher SSIM and lower LPIPS.

TexF is constructed through surface voxelization and texture transfer, whereas UVAtlas requires more complex UV reparameterization and atlas packing.

As shown in Table , TexF construction takes less than 1 s on average even at 4K resolution, and remains below 10 s with refinement.

By contrast, UVAtlas requires approximately 100 s on MPEG and more than 1600 s on the more complex AOM dataset. Overall, TexF reduces representation construction time by orders of magnitude relative to UVAtlas reparameterization.

Among the serialized variants, Serialized-Hilbert offers a modest improvement over Serialized-Morton, but both require substantially more resident memory than 3DNTC. Serialization enables reuse of ASTC, but rearranging voxel attributes into 2D layouts can weaken the spatial correlations available to the codec.

Even without addressing overhead, both serialized ASTC variants require more memory than 3DNTC at matched quality.

Random access also requires a mapping from voxel locations to serialized attributes; even a compact DAG introduces an additional memory cost.

For Serialized-Morton/ASTC, addressing accounts for roughly 50% of the resident memory at the highest texture rate and over 80% at the lowest on both datasets (Fig. ()).

In contrast, 3DNTC uses direct hash addressing without an explicit per-voxel index. These results highlight the importance of both exploiting 3D spatial correlations and limiting addressing overhead, beyond removing UV mapping alone.

As shown in Fig.  and Table , TexF/Unicorn retains its compression advantage without pre-compression IR.

As shown in Fig. , TexF generally achieves larger savings on assets with fewer texels per face, particularly below approximately 100, while UV becomes more competitive at higher ratios.

UV is particularly competitive on the five DCC-authored animation assets, whose relatively coarse meshes incur little UV mapping overhead. Conversely, TexF offers greater gains on densely tessellated scanned assets, where it avoids the larger UV mapping overhead.

Fig.  contrasts Orbiter_space with Winter_girl, a failure case in which TexF requires more storage. These observations suggest that TexF and UV offer complementary strengths, motivating future compression schemes that select between them based on asset characteristics.

16

17

3 IV-E

TexF natively supports direct compression and rendering, but the decoded representation can also be baked into a conventional texture image using a UV atlas generated after decoding. This optional path transmits neither the generated UV data nor the baked texture, so the appearance bitstream remains unchanged.

UV baking reduces the average BD-BR savings by only 1.4 percentage points across the two datasets (Table ), largely retaining TexF’s compression advantage. The R–D curves in Fig.  further show that the quality loss is most noticeable in PSNR at high bitrates. TexF can therefore support conventional UV rendering with limited impact on compression performance, at a one-time conversion cost of approximately 1.6 s on MPEG and 19.8 s on AOM.

II

15

4 IV-E

TexF naturally extends from RGB textures to PBR materials by expanding its attribute channels to include properties such as metallicity and roughness.

The same framework supports PBR rendering and inverse-rendering refinement, with 3DNTC jointly compressing the material channels.

Fig.  compares GT with uncompressed and 3DNTC-compressed TexF renderings of FlightHelmet and WaterBottle from the Khronos glTF Sample Assets. The visual and objective results show that both representations preserve material appearance, demonstrating the feasibility of UV-free PBR representation and compression. A comprehensive study of PBR compression is left for future work.

18

: Fig. 18PBR representation and compression.

IV-FLimitations and Discussion

TexF’s compression advantage depends in part on asset characteristics.

Some DCC-authored assets with coarse geometry and efficiently mapped textures favor UV coding, as shown in Sec. , motivating asset-adaptive representation selection.

Additionally, at coarse voxel resolutions, closely spaced surface regions may map to the same voxel or fall within the same interpolation neighborhood, causing unintended attribute blending.

Developing texture representations and interpolation schemes that better account for local surface structure is a promising direction for mitigating such artifacts.Representation trade-offs.

IV-E2

Although 3DNTC supports low-latency decoding, its per-asset fitting remains costly, making the current encoder better suited to offline asset preparation.

The substantial training acceleration achieved by NTC through a custom GPU implementation  suggests potential for reducing this cost through similar optimizations.

Native TexF rendering currently lacks the full texture-filtering functionality of established UV pipelines.

However, its demonstrated real-time performance provides a foundation for extending native rendering capabilities.

For the bitstream pipeline, decoded TexF can also be baked into a newly generated UV atlas (Sec. ), providing compatibility with existing UV rendering pipelines at a one-time conversion cost while largely retaining the compression gains.Computational cost and rendering support.[]

12

IV-E3

V Conclusion

We introduced TexF, a surface-aligned 3D texture representation for mesh texture compression. TexF avoids explicit UV parameterization, supports efficient construction and direct rendering, and provides a common representation for both bitstream and GPU-resident random-access compression. Experiments on the MPEG and AOM datasets demonstrate improved average rate–distortion performance in both compression settings, a favorable capacity–quality trade-off, and lower construction cost than UV reparameterization. TexF also supports real-time rendering.

Further analyses show that the compression gains persist without rendering-driven optimization and identify asset-dependent trade-offs with UV coding. Optional conversion to UV atlases provides compatibility with existing rendering pipelines. These results position TexF as a complementary 3D-native alternative within existing texture-compression workflows. Future work will explore joint geometry–texture rate allocation and optimization under a shared rendering objective.

We train 3DNTC for 100k steps with an MSE loss against TexF attributes, using batch sizes of 65,536 for $K=2048$ and 262,144 for $K=4096$ . Adam learning rates start at 0.1 for latents and 0.005 for the decoder and follow cosine decay to zero.

We then refine the compressed field using the same IR settings as in the main paper, with the number of iterations increased to 100.

The per-query MAC counts reported in the main paper are computed as follows.

With MLP widths $(2F+18,64,48,32,16)$ , decoding costs $C=144F+6272$ MACs per query, including latent interpolation. This averages 8.96 and 9.96 KMACs on MPEG and AOM, respectively.

Under the same accounting, NTC costs $C_{\mathrm{NTC}}=8192+8F_{\mathrm{NTC}}$ MACs per query, averaging 8.28 KMACs for $F_{\mathrm{NTC}}=(8,12,8,12,16)$ .

S3 Extensions

S3-ATexture Compression under Lossy Geometry

The preceding experiments use lossless geometry to isolate texture compression. We further examine whether TexF retains its advantage under lossy geometry compression. Following the V-DMC CTC , we evaluate all eight MPEG assets and 32 AOM assets at a representative intermediate-rate operating point for geometry compression. and use the same decoded mesh. Quality is evaluated against the original assets, and only texture-related bitstreams are compared, since the geometry payload is shared.[]

30

TexF/UnicornUV-Reparam/HEVC

Fig.  and Table  show that TexF retains substantial bitrate savings under PSNR, SSIM, and 3D-PSNR on both datasets, while LPIPS performance is comparable to the UV baseline on MPEG and improves substantially on AOM. These results indicate that TexF’s compression benefits extend to lossy geometry condition.

S3-BCompatibility with Implicit Geometry

TexF can also represent appearance alongside implicit geometry, extending its use beyond the original mesh. We demonstrate this compatibility by coupling TexF with an SDF and rendering the extracted surface through a standard vertex-color pipeline.

The SDF and TexF share the same grid. After extracting a mesh with Marching Cubes , we transfer TexF attributes to its vertices using $k$ -nearest-neighbor interpolation. The rasterizer then interpolates these vertex attributes across triangles, avoiding per-pixel TexF queries (Fig. ).[]

57

S3

Fig.  shows that TexF/Unicorn (SDF) retains an overall texture compression advantage over UV-Reparam/HEVC on MPEG, although its 3D-PSNR advantage diminishes at higher rates. Relative to the default TexF/Unicorn pipeline, SSIM and LPIPS remain close, whereas PSNR and 3D-PSNR decrease. Geometry and interpolation changes may explain these larger pointwise errors despite similar structural and perceptual quality. Only texture bitstreams are compared; geometry coding is outside this experiment.

S4

This extension supports implicit geometry and vertex-based rendering at some cost in fidelity. The shared grid also suggests a direction for joint geometry and texture compression.

item.title: 屏幕空间反射算法深度分析及其在 URP 中的实现（一） ｜ 深度分析屏幕空间反射算法以及在URP中的实现（一）
item.description:
一句话：从 DDA 步进与光栅化规则讲起，一路落到 URP 延迟渲染里的 SSR 实现。

要点：

  • 先把 DDA 数字微分分析器的直线光栅化规则讲透：按主导方向加一、另一方向做步进判定
  • 用逆光追思路引出屏幕空间反射：从相机发射光线找交点，只在屏幕已有信息里做步进
  • 工程环境明确：Unity 2022.3.60f1c1、URP 14.0.12、延迟渲染，附 GitHub 开源实现，覆盖法线贴图与平滑地面两类表面

为什么值得看：SSR 是「廉价反射」的工业标准做法，把 DDA 步进这一段底层原理讲清楚的文章不多，照着能自己写一遍。

中文摘要：反射是实时渲染里提升画面质感最直接的一环，SSR 则是游戏里最常用的廉价方案。文章是系列第一篇：先补基础理论，把 DDA 数字微分分析器算法的直线光栅化规则讲清楚——先由两点在 XY 上的变化量确定主导方向，步进时主导方向加一、另一方向做光栅化判定；接着概述光线追踪的逆向模拟思路，给出 Whitted 式光追的核心代码骨架（BVH 求交、直接光照、递归深度截断）。在这些基础上再进入屏幕空间反射：为什么只能在屏幕已有信息里做步进、会丢失屏幕外的反射信息。工程侧给出明确环境：Unity 2022.3.60f1c1、URP 14.0.12、延迟渲染路径，附 GitHub 仓库，效果覆盖使用法线贴图的表面与平滑地面两类典型情况。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·UWA（中文）

深度分析屏幕空间反射算法以及在URP中的实现（一）

作者：admin

/

时间：6天前

/

浏览：261 次

/

厚积薄发

【USparkle专栏】如果你深怀绝技，爱“搞点研究”，乐于分享也博采众长，我们期待你的加入，让智慧的火花碰撞交织，让知识的传递生生不息！

前言

湿润的地面，倒映着远方青山，什么样的技术才能造就如此绚丽的效果呢？

本文实现的效果：

使用法线贴图的效果

平滑地面

代码仓库：

GitHub: Screen Space Reflection in URP

Unity版本：2022.3.60f1c1

URP版本：14.0.12

使用延迟渲染

反射一直是实时渲染中十分重要的部分，通常来说，我们觉得画面质感单调，缺少反光，多半是因为没有反射效果。可以看下图对比：

古墓丽影，来自SSR基础介绍[1]

作为实时渲染的一种廉价的反射效果，经常被用在游戏中：

看门狗

看门狗2

巫师3

鸣潮

前置理论基础

DDA算法全称为（Digital Differential Analyzer），是计算机图形学中最基础、最直观的之一。1. DDA数字微分分析器算法直线光栅化算法

首先要明白在显示器上画线本质是画一系列的点，即每一个像素：

如果要光栅化一个3D线段, 应该考虑的就是如何选择XY步进方向, 即确定步进规则：

这段代码翻译过来就是：

先根据两个点的XY分量变化，确定使用一个主导方向。

步进时，在主导方向上进行加一，在另一个方向上进行光栅化判断。

下图展示了当3D线在光栅化后，横向长度大于竖直长度时（即 X1 - X0 > Y1 - Y0），Draw的规则：

同理 X1 - X0 < Y1 - Y0。

2. Ray Tracing概述

光线追踪（Ray Tracing）是计算机图形学中基于物理光学原理的渲染技术，核心思想是模拟光线在三维场景中的传播、反射、折射与吸收过程，计算光线与物体表面的交互，最终生成具有高度真实感的图像。

光线追踪的本质是逆向模拟光的传播路径 —— 由于直接模拟从光源出发的海量光线（多数不会进入相机）效率极低，实际采用的是“从相机/眼睛向场景发射光线去找光源”的逆向思路。

一个基础的光线追踪的核心代码如下：

// 输入：光线、场景、递归深度；输出：光线最终颜色

Vector3 whitted_ray_trace(Ray ray, Scene scene, int depth) {

// 1. 终止条件：递归深度达到上限（避免无限递归）

if (depth > MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH) {

return Vector3(0, 0, 0); // 超出深度，无颜色贡献

}

// 2. 光线与场景求交（用BVH加速，替代遍历所有物体）

HitInfo hit = scene.bvh_root.intersect(ray);

if (!hit.is_hit) {

return scene.background; // 未命中物体，返回背景色

}

// 3. 计算直接光照（光源对交点的直接贡献）

Vector3 direct_light = calculate_direct_light(hit, scene);

// 4. 计算间接光照（反射+折射光线的递归贡献）

Vector3 indirect_light = Vector3(0, 0, 0);

Material mat = hit.material;

// 4.1 生成反射光线（金属/漫反射物体均有反射）

Vector3 reflect_dir = reflect(ray.direction, hit.normal);

Ray reflect_ray = Ray(

hit.point, // 反射光线起点=交点（偏移微小距离避免自相交）

reflect_dir, // 反射方向（单位向量）

1e-4, // t_min=1e-4（避免与自身交点）

INF // t_max=无穷大

);

// 反射颜色贡献=材质反射系数*反射光线递归结果

Vector3 reflect_color = whitted_ray_trace(reflect_ray, scene, depth+1);

indirect_light = indirect_light.add(reflect_color.multiply(mat.albedo));

// 4.2 生成折射光线（仅透明物体如玻璃、水）

if (mat.is_transparent) {

Vector3 refract_dir;

// 判断光线是从外部进入物体（法向量反向）还是内部射出

bool is_inside = ray.direction.dot(hit.normal) > 0;

Vector3 normal = hit.normal;

float eta_i = 1.0; // 入射介质折射率（空气=1.0）

float eta_t = mat.refractive_idx; // 透射介质折射率

if (is_inside) {

normal = normal.multiply(-1); // 内部射出时，法向量反向

swap(eta_i, eta_t); // 交换折射率

}

// 斯涅尔定律计算折射方向（判断是否全反射）

if (refract(ray.direction, normal, eta_i/eta_t, refract_dir)) {

Ray refract_ray = Ray(

hit.point,

refract_dir,

1e-4,

INF

);

// 折射颜色贡献=材质透射系数*折射光线递归结果

Vector3 refract_color = whitted_ray_trace(refract_ray, scene, depth+1);

indirect_light = indirect_light.add(refract_color.multiply(mat.albedo));

} else {

// 全反射：无折射，仅反射（如水中看空气的全反射）

indirect_light = indirect_light.add(reflect_color.multiply(mat.albedo));

}

}

// 5. 合并直接光照与间接光照（返回最终颜色）

return direct_light.add(indirect_light);

}

从代码中，我们可以知道，RayTracing做的事情是针对于全局的，依赖于，并且，求交的算法是针对于每个物体的每个而言的，如果我们要在屏幕空间进行反射处理的话，首先遇到的难点就是。整个场景信息表面（三角形）采样什么，怎么求交

我们怎么在X点拿到P点的信息

针对以上两个问题，我们的SSR给出了十分棒的解决方案。首先，既然是屏幕空间，那么能采样到的信息也必然是屏幕空间的信息，这就不难想到，在Fragment Shader中，针对每一个像素，我们可以在屏幕空间利用深度信息（_CameraDepthRenderTexture）计算出其对应的Shading Point的世界位置，提取法线信息（_CameraNormalRenderTexture），并计算反射后的向量，在反射向量的方向上，我们可以采用步进式采样（Ray Marching）， 通过比较深度缓冲区中的深度图（_CameraDepthRenderTexture）与采样点的深度大小来判断光线是否命中场景表面，命中场景表面的颜色就从我们渲染好的场景图片（_CameraColorRenderTexture）中采样，最后叠加到原图像上。

来自Games 202

总的来说，SSR流程为：

反射光线生成：

屏幕空间投影：

步进采样与命中检测：

反射颜色提取与融合：

既然我们在屏幕空间进行反射处理，那么必然就拿不到所有场景的，也就无法实现真正的Ray Tracing，好在Ray Marching给了我们不错的采样思路。3. Ray Marching几何信息

Ray Marching（光线步进）是计算机图形学中一种基于迭代采样的渲染技术，核心思想是沿光线传播方向“逐步推进”并采样场景，通过判断“当前采样点是否满足终止条件”（如命中物体、超出最大距离）来计算光线与场景的交互。

顾名思义，Ray Marching就是射线一步一步走的意思。从Shading Point开始，向我们反向向量一步一步进行采样计算，如图所示：

。

Games202 ScreenSpaceReflection 39分44秒[2]

单从Ray Marching角度来说，我们需要考虑的就是步长和步进次数，如果步长越大，采样也就越不精准（容易越过交点的表面）， 如果步长过小，那么就会导致过度采样（Over Sampling）， 白白浪费性能，步进次数同理。

高效GPU DDA解决方案的论文中，详细介绍了具体怎么做Ray Marching，这里我们简练地说一下。4. Efﬁcient GPU DDA Solution

如果我们的步进是在世界空间进行的（即在世界空间中是，如下图），那么会出现的两个严重问题：首先，如果我们的Shading Point距离相机远，则我们每次步进对应的其实就是一两个像素，可我们还得进行100来次的采样，这会导致严重的Over Sampling，如下图：均匀步进采样

https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/386510829

如果我们的Shading Point距离我们的相机过近，那么我们一个步长又会导致在屏幕空间中跨度太大，从而使，如下图：精度大大降低

https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/386510829

那么我们如何采样才能最大程度利用起来屏幕信息呢？答案就是把我们的步进过程放到！屏幕空间

https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/386510829

注意：屏幕空间进行Ray Marching丢了深度信息（我们步进到一个像素，我们不知道其步进采样点的深度），因此还需要（学过透视投影就知道不能用Q0到Q1进行线性插值，透视投影矩阵推导：）。单独保存在屏幕空间从H0变化到H1的z值

Games101 MVP变换[3]

为了找到步进采样点的深度，把的Q变换到，保留其w分量，通过透视除法转换到中的V，这样我们就得到了与的成线性关系的坐标了：视线空间裁剪空间NDC空间屏幕空间

之后，把步进采样的坐标转化为NDC空间的V，再反向投影到，此时就可以读取步进出来的深度了：屏幕空间视线空间Q

原文链接：

https://jcgt.org/published/0003/04/04/paper.pdf

知乎猫猫居士介绍此论文：

【论文复现】Efficient GPU Screen-Space Ray Tracing

SSR算法分析与实战

先来一个基本的SSR实现，我们可以用URP管线下的，也可以使用实现，本质都是利用GPU进行运算，本文使用URP管线的RenderFeature来实现SSR效果，对Computer Shader感兴趣的，可以简单看一下。RenderFeature + Blit ShaderMonoBehaviour(C#) + ComputeShader

【Unity教程】小祥带你实现屏幕空间反射SSR_哔哩哔哩_bilibili[4]

这里我使用延迟渲染管线进行渲染，我认为这种基于屏幕空间处理的，和延迟渲染十分搭配，所需要的数据只需要跑一遍pass就全都拿到了，成功把计算和数据读取解耦合，如果要新添加功能也十分容易。值得注意的是，GBuffer2的xyz储存的是世界空间法线，a通道储存的是光滑度信息。

创建Render Pipeline，创建Render Feature：1. 基本配置

using System;

using UnityEngine;

using UnityEngine.Rendering;

using UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal;

using UnityEngine.Serialization;

namespaceScreenSpaceReflection.Render

{

publicclassSsrRenderFeature : ScriptableRendererFeature

{

[Serializable]

publicclassSsrSettings

{

[SerializeField] internalint StepCount = 200;

[SerializeField] internalfloat Thickness = 0.3f;

[SerializeField] internalfloat Stride = 0.1f;

[SerializeField] internalfloat RayOffset = 0.1f;

}

[SerializeField] private Shader m_SsrShader;

[SerializeField] private RenderPassEvent m_RenderPassEvent = RenderPassEvent.AfterRenderingOpaques;

[SerializeField] private SsrSettings m_Settings = new();

private Material m_SsrMaterial;

private SsrRenderPass m_SsrRenderPass;

public override void Create()

{

m_SsrRenderPass ??= new SsrRenderPass();

m_SsrRenderPass.renderPassEvent = m_RenderPassEvent;

if(!m_SsrShader)

m_SsrShader = Shader.Find("Hidden/Universal Render Pipeline/Blit");

m_SsrMaterial = CoreUtils.CreateEngineMaterial(m_SsrShader);

m_SsrRenderPass.Create(m_SsrMaterial);

}

public override void AddRenderPasses(ScriptableRenderer renderer, ref RenderingData renderingData)

{

renderer.EnqueuePass(m_SsrRenderPass);

}

public override void SetupRenderPasses(ScriptableRenderer renderer, in RenderingData renderingData)

{

m_SsrRenderPass.Setup(m_Settings);

}

// 一定要做好内存管理!!!!!

protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)

{

m_SsrRenderPass?.Dispose();

m_SsrRenderPass?.ClearUp();

m_SsrRenderPass = null;

}

}

}

创建C#，来个RenderPass：

using UnityEngine;

using UnityEngine.Experimental.Rendering;

using UnityEngine.Rendering;

using UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal;

namespaceScreenSpaceReflection.Render

{

staticclassSsrShaderConstants

{

publicstaticreadonlystring SsrTexName = "_SsrTex";

publicstaticreadonlyint SsrTexID = Shader.PropertyToID(SsrTexName);

// x: step count, y: thickness, z: step size(Stride)

publicstaticreadonlyint SsrParametersID = Shader.PropertyToID("_SsrParameters");

}

publicclassSsrRenderPass : ScriptableRenderPass

{

privateconststring m_SsrProfilingTag = "SSRRenderPass";

private ProfilingSampler m_ProfilingSampler = new(m_SsrProfilingTag + "_Sampler");

private SsrRenderFeature.SsrSettings m_Settings;

private Material m_SsrMaterial;

private RTHandle m_SourceRT;

private RTHandle m_DestinationRT;

private RTHandle m_SsrRT;

private RenderTextureDescriptor m_Descriptor;

public void Create(Material ssrMaterial)

{

m_SsrMaterial = ssrMaterial;

m_SsrRT = RTHandles.Alloc(SsrShaderConstants.SsrTexID, name: SsrShaderConstants.SsrTexName);

}

public void Setup(SsrRenderFeature.SsrSettings settings)

{

m_Settings = settings;

}

public override void OnCameraSetup(CommandBuffer cmd, ref RenderingData renderingData)

{

m_SourceRT = renderingData.cameraData.renderer.cameraColorTargetHandle;

m_DestinationRT = renderingData.cameraData.renderer.cameraColorTargetHandle;

m_Descriptor = renderingData.cameraData.cameraTargetDescriptor;

m_Descriptor.useMipMap = false;

m_Descriptor.autoGenerateMips = false;

m_SsrMaterial.SetVector(SsrShaderConstants.SsrParametersID,

new Vector4(m_Settings.StepCount, m_Settings.Thickness / 100,

m_Settings.Stride / 100000, m_Settings.RayOffset));

}

public override void Execute(ScriptableRenderContext context, ref RenderingData renderingData)

{

CommandBuffer cmd = CommandBufferPool.Get(m_SsrProfilingTag + "_CommandBuffer");

using (new ProfilingScope(cmd, m_ProfilingSampler))

{

var tempDesc = GetCompatibleDescriptor(m_Descriptor.width, m_Descriptor.height,

GraphicsFormat.B10G11R11_UFloatPack32);

RenderingUtils.ReAllocateIfNeeded(ref m_SsrRT, tempDesc, FilterMode.Bilinear,

TextureWrapMode.Clamp,

name: m_SsrRT.name);

Blitter.BlitCameraTexture(cmd, m_SourceRT, m_SsrRT, RenderBufferLoadAction.DontCare,

RenderBufferStoreAction.Store, m_SsrMaterial, 0);

Blitter.BlitCameraTexture(cmd, m_SsrRT, m_DestinationRT);

}

context.ExecuteCommandBuffer(cmd);

cmd.Clear();

CommandBufferPool.Release(cmd);

}

public override void OnCameraCleanup(CommandBuffer cmd)

{

m_SourceRT = null;

m_DestinationRT = null;

}

// 一定要做好内存管理!!!!!

public void Dispose()

{

m_SsrRT?.Release();

}

public void ClearUp()

{

CoreUtils.Destroy(m_SsrMaterial);

}

RenderTextureDescriptor GetCompatibleDescriptor(int width, int height, GraphicsFormat format,

DepthBits depthBufferBits = DepthBits.None)

=> GetCompatibleDescriptor(m_Descriptor, width, height, format, depthBufferBits);

private static RenderTextureDescriptor GetCompatibleDescriptor(RenderTextureDescriptor desc, int width,

int height, GraphicsFormat format, DepthBits depthBufferBits = DepthBits.None)

{

desc.depthBufferBits = (int)depthBufferBits;

desc.msaaSamples = 1;

desc.width = width;

desc.height = height;

desc.graphicsFormat = format;

return desc;

}

}

}

视图空间Ray Marching

Shader：

// Core.hlsl for XR dependencies

#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/ShaderLibrary/Core.hlsl"

........

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Functions -- -- -- -- -- -

// 函数都放在这里(看下文)

#include "Assets/ScreenSpaceReflection/Shaders/ShaderLib/SsrFunctions.hlsl"

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Uniform Variable -- -- -- -- -- -

SAMPLER(sampler_BlitTexture);

// x : step count, y : thickness, z : step size w : ray offset

float4 _SsrParameters;

#define RAY_OFFSET _SsrParameters.w

#define STEP_COUNT _SsrParameters.x

#define THICKNESS _SsrParameters.y

#define STEP_SIZE _SsrParameters.z

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Shader Stage -- -- -- -- --

half4 SsrFrag(Varyings input) : SV_Target

{

// -- -- -- Base Data -- -- -- --

float2 uv = input.texcoord;

// rawDepth 记录NDC空间的Z信息 [0, 1]

float rawDepth = SampleSceneDepth(uv);

// linearDepth 为视线空间的Z坐标绝对值

// float linear01Depth = Linear01Depth(rawDepth, _ZBufferParams);

float3 normalWS = 0;

float smoothness = 0;

GetNormalAndSmoothness(uv, normalWS, smoothness);

float3 normalVS = TransformWorldToViewDir(normalWS);

float3 posWS = GetWorldSpacePosition(uv, rawDepth);

float3 viewDirWS = normalize(_WorldSpaceCameraPos - posWS);

float3 viewDirVS = TransformWorldToViewDir(viewDirWS);

float3 reflDirWS = normalize(- reflect(viewDirWS, normalWS));

float3 posVS = TransformWorldToView(posWS);

// 存在自反射，需要加一定的偏移

float3 rayVS = posVS + normalVS * RAY_OFFSET;

// -- -- -- Shading -- -- -- -- --

// 视图空间RayMarching

UNITY_LOOP

for (int i = 0; i < STEP_COUNT; i ++)

{

rayVS += reflDirVS * STEP_SIZE * i;

float2 currRayUV;

ReconstructUV(rayVS, currRayUV);

float currSampleDepth = SampleSceneDepth(currRayUV).x;

// 重构出相机空间的Z坐标（绝对值）进行比较，方便调参

float currSampleZ = LinearEyeDepth(currSampleDepth, _ZBufferParams);

float currRayZ = - rayVS.z;

float deltaZ = currRayZ - currSampleZ;

if (deltaZ >= 0 && deltaZ < THICKNESS)

{

// for debug：直接获取到反射的信息

// return GetSource(currRayUV);

return GetSource(currRayUV) * smoothness + GetSource(uv);

}

}

// for debug：未击中的区域为黑色

// return half4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);

return GetSource(uv);

}

Shader Functions:

// 获取Blit Texture

half4 GetSource(float2 uv)

{

return SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X_LOD(_BlitTexture, sampler_LinearRepeat, uv, _BlitMipLevel);

}

// 获取normal

float3 GetNormal(float2 uv)

{

return SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X(_CameraNormalsTexture, sampler_CameraNormalsTexture, uv).xyz;

}

// 在延迟渲染管线的Normal Buffer中，a通道输出的是平滑度

// 获取世界空间的法线和平滑度

void GetNormalAndSmoothness(float2 uv, out float3 normal, out float smoothness)

{

float4 normalAndSmoothness = SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X(_CameraNormalsTexture, sampler_CameraNormalsTexture, uv);

normal = normalize(normalAndSmoothness.xyz);// 在normalize时， 注意不要有w分量

smoothness = normalAndSmoothness.w;

}

// 反投影重建世界坐标

float3 GetWorldSpacePosition(float2 uv, half depth)

{

return ComputeWorldSpacePosition(uv.xy, depth, UNITY_MATRIX_I_VP);

}

// ---------- temp ---------------

// 从视图空间坐标重构屏幕空间的片元uv和深度

void ReconstructUVAndDepth(float3 posWS, out float2 uv, out float depth)

{

half4 posCS = TransformWViewToHClip(posWS);

// posCS.w = -posVS.z

half4 posNDC = posCS / posCS.w;

depth = posNDC.z;

uv = float2(posCS.x, posCS.y * _ProjectionParams.x) / posCS.w * 0.5 + 0.5;

}

// 从视图空间坐标重构屏幕空间的片元uv和深度

void ReconstructUV(float3 posWS, out float2 uv)

{

half4 posCS = TransformWViewToHClip(posWS);

uv = float2(posCS.x, posCS.y * _ProjectionParams.x) / posCS.w * 0.5 + 0.5;

}

问题1：相机向下看时，出现相同颜色的拉丝现象：1. 问题解析

原因其实是我们这一部分已经步进到屏幕外了，采样的点自然也是屏幕外的CameraColor，又由于我们的Warp模式为Clamp，所以采样出来的东西会显示一大长条相同颜色的拉丝，这只需要在我们步进时，检查uv是否到屏幕外就能解决这个问题：

UNITY_LOOP

for (int i = 0; i < STEP_COUNT; i++)

{

.........

ReconstructUV(rayVS, currRayUV);

if (any(currRayUV < 0.0) || any(currRayUV > 1.0))

// for debug：超出屏幕外的返回黑色

return half4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);

// return GetSource(uv);

float currSampleDepth = SampleSceneDepth(currRayUV).x;

.........

}

问题2：分级拉丝

这个问题还是比较难以理解的，简单来说就是Stride（步长）太大，高频的细节对不齐，无法完全精确捕捉到像素级别的信息，而我的解决办法就是直接拉小步长，同时提高Step Count：

高频细节出来了

性能？

2. 性能分析

参数：

这是我后期改的参数，往下看文章就明白了

我用Profiler大体测了一下执行时间，基本上都是0.58ms~0.61ms。

屏幕空间Ray Marching

视图空间步进还是太浪费了，想要高频细节必须要把控很小的Stride，导致很多步骤都是没用的，也就是Over Sample，溯其本源，我们是在屏幕空间做Ray Marching，那么就最大程度地利用好屏幕信息。

先上一段核心代码（不必细抠细节，先看个大概过程），我想重点讲解几个细节：

// 视图空间 ---> 屏幕空间 (默认是点)

float2 TransformViewToScreen(float3 posVS, float2 screenSize,out float InvW)

{

float4 posCS = TransformWViewToHClip(posVS);

InvW = 1 / posCS.w;

float2 uv = float2(posCS.x, posCS.y * _ProjectionParams.x) / posCS.w * 0.5 + 0.5;

return uv * screenSize;

}

// 屏幕空间RayMarching

float3 ScreenSpaceRayMarching(float2 uv, float3 posVS, float3 reflDirVS, float3 normalVS, float smoothness,

float stepCount, float thickness, float stride, float rayOffset, float maxDistance)

{

// 视图空间中射线起始位置和结束位置

float3 startVS = posVS;

float3 endVS = posVS + reflDirVS * maxDistance;

// inverse w

// w = -Vz，为了后面方便在屏幕空间插值深度

float startInvW = 0;

float endInvW = 0;

// 屏幕空间中射线起始位置和结束位置

// 其实 startSS = uv * _ScreenSize.xy ([0, 1]^2 -> [0, w-1],[0, h-1])

// 但是为了拿到裁剪空间的w分量, 我们必须使用自定义的TransformViewToScreen函数

float2 startSS = TransformViewToScreen(startVS, _ScreenSize.xy, startInvW);

float2 endSS = TransformViewToScreen(endVS, _ScreenSize.xy, endInvW);

// DDA算法

float2 deltaSS = endSS - startSS; // 注意方向性！

bool isVertical = false;

// 我们默认的是以横轴为主导向，如果纵轴为主导向，则进行反转，并在之后进行复原

if (abs(deltaSS.x) < abs(deltaSS.y))

{

isVertical = true;

deltaSS = deltaSS.yx;

startSS = startSS.yx;

endSS = endSS.yx;

}

// 计算屏幕坐标、inverse-w的线性增量

float dir = sign(deltaSS.x); // 屏幕空间增量方向

float invdx = dir / deltaSS.x; // 1 / 屏幕空间增量 (绝对值)

float2 dPosSS = float2(dir, invdx * deltaSS.y);

float dInvW = (endInvW - startInvW) * invdx;

// 步长的调整

dPosSS *= stride;

dInvW *= stride;

// 存在自反射，需要加一定的偏移

float3 rayVS = posVS + normalVS * rayOffset;

float preZ = rayVS.z;// 作为初始 Z 分量和缓存的作用

// 起始数据

float2 currPosSS = startSS;

float currInvW = startInvW;

// RayMarching

UNITY_LOOP

for (int i = 0; i < stepCount && currPosSS.x * dir <= endSS.x * dir; i++)

{

// 缓存前后两步视图空间的Z分量（防止跨像素太大，判断不出相交）

float rayNearZ = preZ;

float rayFarZ = -1 / (dInvW * 0.5 + currInvW);// 初始做一次半步长迈进

preZ = rayFarZ;

// 视图空间中相机朝向-Z方向

if (rayNearZ < rayFarZ)

Swap(rayNearZ, rayFarZ);

// 步近

currPosSS += dPosSS;

currInvW += dInvW;

// 得到交点uv

float2 hitUV = isVertical ? currPosSS.yx : currPosSS; // 复原

hitUV *= _ScreenSize.zw;

if (any(hitUV < 0.0) || any(hitUV > 1.0))

break;

// 相交判断

float surfaceZ = -LinearEyeDepth(SampleSceneDepth(hitUV), _ZBufferParams);

bool intersecting = (rayFarZ <= surfaceZ) && (rayNearZ >= surfaceZ - thickness);

if (intersecting)

// return GetSource(hitUV);

return GetSource(hitUV) * smoothness + GetSource(uv);

}

// return half4(0, 0, 0, 1);

return GetSource(uv);

}

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Shader Stage -- -- -- -- --

half4 SsrFrag(Varyings input) : SV_Target

{

.......

float3 posVS = TransformWorldToView(posWS);

float3 finalColor = ScreenSpaceRayMarching(uv, posVS, reflDirVS, normalVS, smoothness,

STEP_COUNT, THICKNESS, STRIDE, RAY_OFFSET, MAX_DISTANCE);

return half4(finalColor, 1);

}

参数：

效果：

Debug

效果达标！

首先，防止你忘记不同空间的坐标变换，我让豆老师跑出一份Unity中的坐标转换关系：1. 坐标系转换

视图空间与裁剪空间的转换

裁剪空间中的w分量实质上就是视线空间的z分量的相反数（小知识：如果我们把视线空间的xy分量除以裁剪空间中的w分量，得到的坐标中xy分量一定与NDC坐标成线性关系！）。

NDC空间与视图空间的转换

视线空间的z分量与NDC空间中的z分量不成线性关系，但是视线空间中的！1/z是与NDC空间中的z分量成线性关系的

屏幕空间与NDC空间的转换

从上面几个式子中可以看出来，屏幕空间z分量和视图空间1/z分量成（Unity中，经过变换之后的屏幕空间坐标的原点是在左上角，故我们应该对其进行反转），这也就是为什么我在屏幕空间插值的是1/z，而不是z。我们使用1/z可以轻松复原视图空间的z分量。线性关系

1）为什么屏幕空间要用[0, w-1]，[0, h-1]？

其实我开始看别人代码的时候想的是为什么不用[0, 1]范围的uv坐标，如果这样也方便采样，不用重新反向映射一次，直到我看到DDA算法要（float invdx = dir / deltaSS.x;），我才反应过来。实际上我们横纵范围不能看作一样的，我们屏幕分辨率是不同的（全高清1920×1080，四倍高清2560×1440 ...），想要步进屏幕空间，必须精确到像素级别！2. 重点细节讲解算1/屏幕空间增量

2）为什么循环中做一次初始半步长迈进？

从我们的相交判断条件来看：

判断rayFarZ这个较远点是否被表面遮挡；

判断rayNearZ是否在一定阈值（Thickness）内。

只有两个都满足时，才能说明相交成功，进行采样。那么我们先迈进半步长，之后的判断都在Reflection Dir方向的半步长处进行步进，如下图：

这样是十分舒服的判断，既可以防止首次的判断失误，又确保后面的判断正确！

3）为什么要这个Thickness这个阈值？

其实就是增大容错率，如下图：

1）相机向下看时，会有一个自反射圆圈，超出MaxDistance之后会消失。3. 问题解析

这个问题我仔细分析了一下，原因是在视图空间中，我们反射出来的最终位置，可能超出近裁面了，我们如果把这个点映射到屏幕空间就会出错（仔细思考MVP变换，如果有个点在你相机后面（不在视锥体内），变换之后的位置必然不在投影盒中，那么映射到屏幕空间必然会出错），所以我们必须要对这个最终反射点进行一次近裁剪面的判断，从而调整反射点的最终位置，如下：

// 视图空间中射线起始位置和结束位置

float3 startVS = posVS;

float3 endVS = posVS + reflDirVS * maxDistance;

if (endVS.z > -_ProjectionParams.y)

maxDistance = (-_ProjectionParams.y - startVS.z) / reflDirVS.z;

endVS = startVS + reflDirVS * maxDistance;

// inverse w

......

2）屏幕信息缺失

很好理解，毕竟我们在屏幕空间进行反射，那么必定会缺失信息，如下图：

根据Games 202，闫老师给的思路，在屏幕空间进行一次衰减，不同的是，闫老师的思路是利用反射距离进行衰减，我的思路是利用反射点的uv进行衰减。

那么实现步骤也是十分简单的，先在Render Pass传入一个控制衰减的参数attenuation，在Shader中，我使用暗角后处理的控制方法，如下：

if (intersecting)

{

float2 attUV = abs(hitUV - 0.5) * 1.8;

attUV = pow(saturate(attUV), attenuation);

float att = length(attUV);

float edgeFading= pow(saturate(1 - att * att), 5);

return GetSource(hitUV) * smoothness * edgeFading + GetSource(uv);

}

这个效果简单来说就是做一次屏幕边缘的衰减，我的想法就是，如果我们hitUV打到了屏幕边缘，那么就肯定给一个小的权重，若打到屏幕中心，那么肯定要给一个大点的权重，同时需要考虑到屏幕长宽的影响，综合考虑之后，我决定使用暗角作为权重。

一句话：从 DDA 步进与光栅化规则讲起，一路落到 URP 延迟渲染里的 SSR 实现。

要点：

  • 先把 DDA 数字微分分析器的直线光栅化规则讲透：按主导方向加一、另一方向做步进判定
  • 用逆光追思路引出屏幕空间反射：从相机发射光线找交点，只在屏幕已有信息里做步进
  • 工程环境明确：Unity 2022.3.60f1c1、URP 14.0.12、延迟渲染，附 GitHub 开源实现，覆盖法线贴图与平滑地面两类表面

为什么值得看：SSR 是「廉价反射」的工业标准做法，把 DDA 步进这一段底层原理讲清楚的文章不多，照着能自己写一遍。

中文摘要：反射是实时渲染里提升画面质感最直接的一环，SSR 则是游戏里最常用的廉价方案。文章是系列第一篇：先补基础理论，把 DDA 数字微分分析器算法的直线光栅化规则讲清楚——先由两点在 XY 上的变化量确定主导方向，步进时主导方向加一、另一方向做光栅化判定；接着概述光线追踪的逆向模拟思路，给出 Whitted 式光追的核心代码骨架（BVH 求交、直接光照、递归深度截断）。在这些基础上再进入屏幕空间反射：为什么只能在屏幕已有信息里做步进、会丢失屏幕外的反射信息。工程侧给出明确环境：Unity 2022.3.60f1c1、URP 14.0.12、延迟渲染路径，附 GitHub 仓库，效果覆盖使用法线贴图的表面与平滑地面两类典型情况。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·UWA（中文）

深度分析屏幕空间反射算法以及在URP中的实现（一）

作者：admin

/

时间：6天前

/

浏览：261 次

/

厚积薄发

【USparkle专栏】如果你深怀绝技，爱“搞点研究”，乐于分享也博采众长，我们期待你的加入，让智慧的火花碰撞交织，让知识的传递生生不息！

前言

湿润的地面，倒映着远方青山，什么样的技术才能造就如此绚丽的效果呢？

本文实现的效果：

使用法线贴图的效果

平滑地面

代码仓库：

GitHub: Screen Space Reflection in URP

Unity版本：2022.3.60f1c1

URP版本：14.0.12

使用延迟渲染

反射一直是实时渲染中十分重要的部分，通常来说，我们觉得画面质感单调，缺少反光，多半是因为没有反射效果。可以看下图对比：

古墓丽影，来自SSR基础介绍[1]

作为实时渲染的一种廉价的反射效果，经常被用在游戏中：

看门狗

看门狗2

巫师3

鸣潮

前置理论基础

DDA算法全称为（Digital Differential Analyzer），是计算机图形学中最基础、最直观的之一。1. DDA数字微分分析器算法直线光栅化算法

首先要明白在显示器上画线本质是画一系列的点，即每一个像素：

2. Ray Tracing概述

光线追踪（Ray Tracing）是计算机图形学中基于物理光学原理的渲染技术，核心思想是模拟光线在三维场景中的传播、反射、折射与吸收过程，计算光线与物体表面的交互，最终生成具有高度真实感的图像。

光线追踪的本质是逆向模拟光的传播路径 —— 由于直接模拟从光源出发的海量光线（多数不会进入相机）效率极低，实际采用的是“从相机/眼睛向场景发射光线去找光源”的逆向思路。

一个基础的光线追踪的核心代码如下：

// 输入：光线、场景、递归深度；输出：光线最终颜色

Vector3 whitted_ray_trace(Ray ray, Scene scene, int depth) {

// 1. 终止条件：递归深度达到上限（避免无限递归）

if (depth > MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH) {

return Vector3(0, 0, 0); // 超出深度，无颜色贡献

}

// 2. 光线与场景求交（用BVH加速，替代遍历所有物体）

HitInfo hit = scene.bvh_root.intersect(ray);

if (!hit.is_hit) {

return scene.background; // 未命中物体，返回背景色

}

// 3. 计算直接光照（光源对交点的直接贡献）

Vector3 direct_light = calculate_direct_light(hit, scene);

// 4. 计算间接光照（反射+折射光线的递归贡献）

Vector3 indirect_light = Vector3(0, 0, 0);

Material mat = hit.material;

// 4.1 生成反射光线（金属/漫反射物体均有反射）

Vector3 reflect_dir = reflect(ray.direction, hit.normal);

Ray reflect_ray = Ray(

hit.point, // 反射光线起点=交点（偏移微小距离避免自相交）

reflect_dir, // 反射方向（单位向量）

1e-4, // t_min=1e-4（避免与自身交点）

INF // t_max=无穷大

);

// 反射颜色贡献=材质反射系数*反射光线递归结果

Vector3 reflect_color = whitted_ray_trace(reflect_ray, scene, depth+1);

indirect_light = indirect_light.add(reflect_color.multiply(mat.albedo));

// 4.2 生成折射光线（仅透明物体如玻璃、水）

if (mat.is_transparent) {

Vector3 refract_dir;

// 判断光线是从外部进入物体（法向量反向）还是内部射出

bool is_inside = ray.direction.dot(hit.normal) > 0;

Vector3 normal = hit.normal;

float eta_i = 1.0; // 入射介质折射率（空气=1.0）

float eta_t = mat.refractive_idx; // 透射介质折射率

if (is_inside) {

normal = normal.multiply(-1); // 内部射出时，法向量反向

swap(eta_i, eta_t); // 交换折射率

}

// 斯涅尔定律计算折射方向（判断是否全反射）

if (refract(ray.direction, normal, eta_i/eta_t, refract_dir)) {

Ray refract_ray = Ray(

hit.point,

refract_dir,

1e-4,

INF

);

// 折射颜色贡献=材质透射系数*折射光线递归结果

Vector3 refract_color = whitted_ray_trace(refract_ray, scene, depth+1);

indirect_light = indirect_light.add(refract_color.multiply(mat.albedo));

} else {

// 全反射：无折射，仅反射（如水中看空气的全反射）

indirect_light = indirect_light.add(reflect_color.multiply(mat.albedo));

}

}

// 5. 合并直接光照与间接光照（返回最终颜色）

return direct_light.add(indirect_light);

}

从代码中，我们可以知道，RayTracing做的事情是针对于全局的，依赖于，并且，求交的算法是针对于每个物体的每个而言的，如果我们要在屏幕空间进行反射处理的话，首先遇到的难点就是。整个场景信息表面（三角形）采样什么，怎么求交

我们怎么在X点拿到P点的信息

针对以上两个问题，我们的SSR给出了十分棒的解决方案。首先，既然是屏幕空间，那么能采样到的信息也必然是屏幕空间的信息，这就不难想到，在Fragment Shader中，针对每一个像素，我们可以在屏幕空间利用深度信息（_CameraDepthRenderTexture）计算出其对应的Shading Point的世界位置，提取法线信息（_CameraNormalRenderTexture），并计算反射后的向量，在反射向量的方向上，我们可以采用步进式采样（Ray Marching）， 通过比较深度缓冲区中的深度图（_CameraDepthRenderTexture）与采样点的深度大小来判断光线是否命中场景表面，命中场景表面的颜色就从我们渲染好的场景图片（_CameraColorRenderTexture）中采样，最后叠加到原图像上。

既然我们在屏幕空间进行反射处理，那么必然就拿不到所有场景的，也就无法实现真正的Ray Tracing，好在Ray Marching给了我们不错的采样思路。3. Ray Marching几何信息

Ray Marching（光线步进）是计算机图形学中一种基于迭代采样的渲染技术，核心思想是沿光线传播方向“逐步推进”并采样场景，通过判断“当前采样点是否满足终止条件”（如命中物体、超出最大距离）来计算光线与场景的交互。

顾名思义，Ray Marching就是射线一步一步走的意思。从Shading Point开始，向我们反向向量一步一步进行采样计算，如图所示：

。

Games202 ScreenSpaceReflection 39分44秒[2]

单从Ray Marching角度来说，我们需要考虑的就是步长和步进次数，如果步长越大，采样也就越不精准（容易越过交点的表面）， 如果步长过小，那么就会导致过度采样（Over Sampling）， 白白浪费性能，步进次数同理。

高效GPU DDA解决方案的论文中，详细介绍了具体怎么做Ray Marching，这里我们简练地说一下。4. Efﬁcient GPU DDA Solution

如果我们的步进是在世界空间进行的（即在世界空间中是，如下图），那么会出现的两个严重问题：首先，如果我们的Shading Point距离相机远，则我们每次步进对应的其实就是一两个像素，可我们还得进行100来次的采样，这会导致严重的Over Sampling，如下图：均匀步进采样

https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/386510829

如果我们的Shading Point距离我们的相机过近，那么我们一个步长又会导致在屏幕空间中跨度太大，从而使，如下图：精度大大降低

https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/386510829

那么我们如何采样才能最大程度利用起来屏幕信息呢？答案就是把我们的步进过程放到！屏幕空间

https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/386510829

注意：屏幕空间进行Ray Marching丢了深度信息（我们步进到一个像素，我们不知道其步进采样点的深度），因此还需要（学过透视投影就知道不能用Q0到Q1进行线性插值，透视投影矩阵推导：）。单独保存在屏幕空间从H0变化到H1的z值

为了找到步进采样点的深度，把的Q变换到，保留其w分量，通过透视除法转换到中的V，这样我们就得到了与的成线性关系的坐标了：视线空间裁剪空间NDC空间屏幕空间

之后，把步进采样的坐标转化为NDC空间的V，再反向投影到，此时就可以读取步进出来的深度了：屏幕空间视线空间Q

这里我使用延迟渲染管线进行渲染，我认为这种基于屏幕空间处理的，和延迟渲染十分搭配，所需要的数据只需要跑一遍pass就全都拿到了，成功把计算和数据读取解耦合，如果要新添加功能也十分容易。值得注意的是，GBuffer2的xyz储存的是世界空间法线，a通道储存的是光滑度信息。

创建Render Pipeline，创建Render Feature：1. 基本配置

using System;

using UnityEngine;

using UnityEngine.Rendering;

using UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal;

using UnityEngine.Serialization;

namespaceScreenSpaceReflection.Render

{

publicclassSsrRenderFeature : ScriptableRendererFeature

{

[Serializable]

publicclassSsrSettings

{

[SerializeField] internalint StepCount = 200;

[SerializeField] internalfloat Thickness = 0.3f;

[SerializeField] internalfloat Stride = 0.1f;

[SerializeField] internalfloat RayOffset = 0.1f;

}

[SerializeField] private Shader m_SsrShader;

[SerializeField] private RenderPassEvent m_RenderPassEvent = RenderPassEvent.AfterRenderingOpaques;

[SerializeField] private SsrSettings m_Settings = new();

private Material m_SsrMaterial;

private SsrRenderPass m_SsrRenderPass;

public override void Create()

{

m_SsrRenderPass ??= new SsrRenderPass();

m_SsrRenderPass.renderPassEvent = m_RenderPassEvent;

if(!m_SsrShader)

m_SsrShader = Shader.Find("Hidden/Universal Render Pipeline/Blit");

m_SsrMaterial = CoreUtils.CreateEngineMaterial(m_SsrShader);

m_SsrRenderPass.Create(m_SsrMaterial);

}

public override void AddRenderPasses(ScriptableRenderer renderer, ref RenderingData renderingData)

{

renderer.EnqueuePass(m_SsrRenderPass);

}

public override void SetupRenderPasses(ScriptableRenderer renderer, in RenderingData renderingData)

{

m_SsrRenderPass.Setup(m_Settings);

}

// 一定要做好内存管理!!!!!

protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)

{

m_SsrRenderPass?.Dispose();

m_SsrRenderPass?.ClearUp();

m_SsrRenderPass = null;

}

}

}

创建C#，来个RenderPass：

using UnityEngine;

using UnityEngine.Experimental.Rendering;

using UnityEngine.Rendering;

using UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal;

namespaceScreenSpaceReflection.Render

{

staticclassSsrShaderConstants

{

publicstaticreadonlystring SsrTexName = "_SsrTex";

publicstaticreadonlyint SsrTexID = Shader.PropertyToID(SsrTexName);

// x: step count, y: thickness, z: step size(Stride)

publicstaticreadonlyint SsrParametersID = Shader.PropertyToID("_SsrParameters");

}

publicclassSsrRenderPass : ScriptableRenderPass

{

privateconststring m_SsrProfilingTag = "SSRRenderPass";

private ProfilingSampler m_ProfilingSampler = new(m_SsrProfilingTag + "_Sampler");

private SsrRenderFeature.SsrSettings m_Settings;

private Material m_SsrMaterial;

private RTHandle m_SourceRT;

private RTHandle m_DestinationRT;

private RTHandle m_SsrRT;

private RenderTextureDescriptor m_Descriptor;

public void Create(Material ssrMaterial)

{

m_SsrMaterial = ssrMaterial;

m_SsrRT = RTHandles.Alloc(SsrShaderConstants.SsrTexID, name: SsrShaderConstants.SsrTexName);

}

public void Setup(SsrRenderFeature.SsrSettings settings)

{

m_Settings = settings;

}

public override void OnCameraSetup(CommandBuffer cmd, ref RenderingData renderingData)

{

m_SourceRT = renderingData.cameraData.renderer.cameraColorTargetHandle;

m_DestinationRT = renderingData.cameraData.renderer.cameraColorTargetHandle;

m_Descriptor = renderingData.cameraData.cameraTargetDescriptor;

m_Descriptor.useMipMap = false;

m_Descriptor.autoGenerateMips = false;

m_SsrMaterial.SetVector(SsrShaderConstants.SsrParametersID,

new Vector4(m_Settings.StepCount, m_Settings.Thickness / 100,

m_Settings.Stride / 100000, m_Settings.RayOffset));

}

public override void Execute(ScriptableRenderContext context, ref RenderingData renderingData)

{

CommandBuffer cmd = CommandBufferPool.Get(m_SsrProfilingTag + "_CommandBuffer");

using (new ProfilingScope(cmd, m_ProfilingSampler))

{

var tempDesc = GetCompatibleDescriptor(m_Descriptor.width, m_Descriptor.height,

GraphicsFormat.B10G11R11_UFloatPack32);

RenderingUtils.ReAllocateIfNeeded(ref m_SsrRT, tempDesc, FilterMode.Bilinear,

TextureWrapMode.Clamp,

name: m_SsrRT.name);

Blitter.BlitCameraTexture(cmd, m_SourceRT, m_SsrRT, RenderBufferLoadAction.DontCare,

RenderBufferStoreAction.Store, m_SsrMaterial, 0);

Blitter.BlitCameraTexture(cmd, m_SsrRT, m_DestinationRT);

}

context.ExecuteCommandBuffer(cmd);

cmd.Clear();

CommandBufferPool.Release(cmd);

}

public override void OnCameraCleanup(CommandBuffer cmd)

{

m_SourceRT = null;

m_DestinationRT = null;

}

// 一定要做好内存管理!!!!!

public void Dispose()

{

m_SsrRT?.Release();

}

public void ClearUp()

{

CoreUtils.Destroy(m_SsrMaterial);

}

RenderTextureDescriptor GetCompatibleDescriptor(int width, int height, GraphicsFormat format,

DepthBits depthBufferBits = DepthBits.None)

=> GetCompatibleDescriptor(m_Descriptor, width, height, format, depthBufferBits);

private static RenderTextureDescriptor GetCompatibleDescriptor(RenderTextureDescriptor desc, int width,

int height, GraphicsFormat format, DepthBits depthBufferBits = DepthBits.None)

{

desc.depthBufferBits = (int)depthBufferBits;

desc.msaaSamples = 1;

desc.width = width;

desc.height = height;

desc.graphicsFormat = format;

return desc;

}

}

}

#pragma vertex Vert

#pragma multi_compile_fragment _ DEBUG_DISPLAY

// Core.hlsl for XR dependencies

#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/ShaderLibrary/Core.hlsl"

#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.core/Runtime/Utilities/Blit.hlsl"

half4 Fragment(Varyings input) : SV_Target

{

UNITY_SETUP_STEREO_EYE_INDEX_POST_VERTEX(input);

float2 uv = input.texcoord;

half4 col = SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X(_BlitTexture, sampler_BlitTexture, uv);

#ifdef _LINEAR_TO_SRGB_CONVERSION

col = LinearToSRGB(col);

#endif

#if defined(DEBUG_DISPLAY)

half4 debugColor = 0;

if(CanDebugOverrideOutputColor(col, uv, debugColor))

{

return debugColor;

}

#endif

return col;

}

ENDHLSL

}

}

}

Shader：

// Core.hlsl for XR dependencies

#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/ShaderLibrary/Core.hlsl"

........

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Functions -- -- -- -- -- -

// 函数都放在这里(看下文)

#include "Assets/ScreenSpaceReflection/Shaders/ShaderLib/SsrFunctions.hlsl"

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Uniform Variable -- -- -- -- -- -

SAMPLER(sampler_BlitTexture);

// x : step count, y : thickness, z : step size w : ray offset

float4 _SsrParameters;

#define RAY_OFFSET _SsrParameters.w

#define STEP_COUNT _SsrParameters.x

#define THICKNESS _SsrParameters.y

#define STEP_SIZE _SsrParameters.z

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Shader Stage -- -- -- -- --

half4 SsrFrag(Varyings input) : SV_Target

{

// -- -- -- Base Data -- -- -- --

float2 uv = input.texcoord;

// rawDepth 记录NDC空间的Z信息 [0, 1]

float rawDepth = SampleSceneDepth(uv);

// linearDepth 为视线空间的Z坐标绝对值

// float linear01Depth = Linear01Depth(rawDepth, _ZBufferParams);

float3 normalWS = 0;

float smoothness = 0;

GetNormalAndSmoothness(uv, normalWS, smoothness);

float3 normalVS = TransformWorldToViewDir(normalWS);

float3 posWS = GetWorldSpacePosition(uv, rawDepth);

float3 viewDirWS = normalize(_WorldSpaceCameraPos - posWS);

float3 viewDirVS = TransformWorldToViewDir(viewDirWS);

float3 reflDirWS = normalize(- reflect(viewDirWS, normalWS));

float3 posVS = TransformWorldToView(posWS);

// 存在自反射，需要加一定的偏移

float3 rayVS = posVS + normalVS * RAY_OFFSET;

// -- -- -- Shading -- -- -- -- --

// 视图空间RayMarching

UNITY_LOOP

for (int i = 0; i < STEP_COUNT; i ++)

{

rayVS += reflDirVS * STEP_SIZE * i;

float2 currRayUV;

ReconstructUV(rayVS, currRayUV);

float currSampleDepth = SampleSceneDepth(currRayUV).x;

// 重构出相机空间的Z坐标（绝对值）进行比较，方便调参

float currSampleZ = LinearEyeDepth(currSampleDepth, _ZBufferParams);

float currRayZ = - rayVS.z;

float deltaZ = currRayZ - currSampleZ;

if (deltaZ >= 0 && deltaZ < THICKNESS)

{

// for debug：直接获取到反射的信息

// return GetSource(currRayUV);

return GetSource(currRayUV) * smoothness + GetSource(uv);

}

}

// for debug：未击中的区域为黑色

// return half4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);

return GetSource(uv);

}

Shader Functions:

// 获取Blit Texture

half4 GetSource(float2 uv)

{

return SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X_LOD(_BlitTexture, sampler_LinearRepeat, uv, _BlitMipLevel);

}

// 获取normal

float3 GetNormal(float2 uv)

{

return SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X(_CameraNormalsTexture, sampler_CameraNormalsTexture, uv).xyz;

}

// 在延迟渲染管线的Normal Buffer中，a通道输出的是平滑度

// 获取世界空间的法线和平滑度

void GetNormalAndSmoothness(float2 uv, out float3 normal, out float smoothness)

{

float4 normalAndSmoothness = SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_X(_CameraNormalsTexture, sampler_CameraNormalsTexture, uv);

normal = normalize(normalAndSmoothness.xyz);// 在normalize时， 注意不要有w分量

smoothness = normalAndSmoothness.w;

}

// 反投影重建世界坐标

float3 GetWorldSpacePosition(float2 uv, half depth)

{

return ComputeWorldSpacePosition(uv.xy, depth, UNITY_MATRIX_I_VP);

}

// ---------- temp ---------------

// 从视图空间坐标重构屏幕空间的片元uv和深度

void ReconstructUVAndDepth(float3 posWS, out float2 uv, out float depth)

{

half4 posCS = TransformWViewToHClip(posWS);

// posCS.w = -posVS.z

half4 posNDC = posCS / posCS.w;

depth = posNDC.z;

uv = float2(posCS.x, posCS.y * _ProjectionParams.x) / posCS.w * 0.5 + 0.5;

}

// 从视图空间坐标重构屏幕空间的片元uv和深度

void ReconstructUV(float3 posWS, out float2 uv)

{

half4 posCS = TransformWViewToHClip(posWS);

uv = float2(posCS.x, posCS.y * _ProjectionParams.x) / posCS.w * 0.5 + 0.5;

}

屏幕空间Ray Marching

视图空间步进还是太浪费了，想要高频细节必须要把控很小的Stride，导致很多步骤都是没用的，也就是Over Sample，溯其本源，我们是在屏幕空间做Ray Marching，那么就最大程度地利用好屏幕信息。

先上一段核心代码（不必细抠细节，先看个大概过程），我想重点讲解几个细节：

// 视图空间 ---> 屏幕空间 (默认是点)

float2 TransformViewToScreen(float3 posVS, float2 screenSize,out float InvW)

{

float4 posCS = TransformWViewToHClip(posVS);

InvW = 1 / posCS.w;

float2 uv = float2(posCS.x, posCS.y * _ProjectionParams.x) / posCS.w * 0.5 + 0.5;

return uv * screenSize;

}

// 屏幕空间RayMarching

float3 ScreenSpaceRayMarching(float2 uv, float3 posVS, float3 reflDirVS, float3 normalVS, float smoothness,

float stepCount, float thickness, float stride, float rayOffset, float maxDistance)

{

// 视图空间中射线起始位置和结束位置

float3 startVS = posVS;

float3 endVS = posVS + reflDirVS * maxDistance;

// inverse w

// w = -Vz，为了后面方便在屏幕空间插值深度

float startInvW = 0;

float endInvW = 0;

// 屏幕空间中射线起始位置和结束位置

// 其实 startSS = uv * _ScreenSize.xy ([0, 1]^2 -> [0, w-1],[0, h-1])

// 但是为了拿到裁剪空间的w分量, 我们必须使用自定义的TransformViewToScreen函数

float2 startSS = TransformViewToScreen(startVS, _ScreenSize.xy, startInvW);

float2 endSS = TransformViewToScreen(endVS, _ScreenSize.xy, endInvW);

// DDA算法

float2 deltaSS = endSS - startSS; // 注意方向性！

bool isVertical = false;

// 我们默认的是以横轴为主导向，如果纵轴为主导向，则进行反转，并在之后进行复原

if (abs(deltaSS.x) < abs(deltaSS.y))

{

isVertical = true;

deltaSS = deltaSS.yx;

startSS = startSS.yx;

endSS = endSS.yx;

}

// 计算屏幕坐标、inverse-w的线性增量

float dir = sign(deltaSS.x); // 屏幕空间增量方向

float invdx = dir / deltaSS.x; // 1 / 屏幕空间增量 (绝对值)

float2 dPosSS = float2(dir, invdx * deltaSS.y);

float dInvW = (endInvW - startInvW) * invdx;

// 步长的调整

dPosSS *= stride;

dInvW *= stride;

// 存在自反射，需要加一定的偏移

float3 rayVS = posVS + normalVS * rayOffset;

float preZ = rayVS.z;// 作为初始 Z 分量和缓存的作用

// 起始数据

float2 currPosSS = startSS;

float currInvW = startInvW;

// RayMarching

UNITY_LOOP

for (int i = 0; i < stepCount && currPosSS.x * dir <= endSS.x * dir; i++)

{

// 缓存前后两步视图空间的Z分量（防止跨像素太大，判断不出相交）

float rayNearZ = preZ;

float rayFarZ = -1 / (dInvW * 0.5 + currInvW);// 初始做一次半步长迈进

preZ = rayFarZ;

// 视图空间中相机朝向-Z方向

if (rayNearZ < rayFarZ)

Swap(rayNearZ, rayFarZ);

// 步近

currPosSS += dPosSS;

currInvW += dInvW;

// 得到交点uv

float2 hitUV = isVertical ? currPosSS.yx : currPosSS; // 复原

hitUV *= _ScreenSize.zw;

if (any(hitUV < 0.0) || any(hitUV > 1.0))

break;

// 相交判断

float surfaceZ = -LinearEyeDepth(SampleSceneDepth(hitUV), _ZBufferParams);

bool intersecting = (rayFarZ <= surfaceZ) && (rayNearZ >= surfaceZ - thickness);

if (intersecting)

// return GetSource(hitUV);

return GetSource(hitUV) * smoothness + GetSource(uv);

}

// return half4(0, 0, 0, 1);

return GetSource(uv);

}

// -- -- -- -- -- -- Shader Stage -- -- -- -- --

half4 SsrFrag(Varyings input) : SV_Target

{

.......

float3 posVS = TransformWorldToView(posWS);

float3 finalColor = ScreenSpaceRayMarching(uv, posVS, reflDirVS, normalVS, smoothness,

STEP_COUNT, THICKNESS, STRIDE, RAY_OFFSET, MAX_DISTANCE);

return half4(finalColor, 1);

}

参数：

效果：

Debug

效果达标！

首先，防止你忘记不同空间的坐标变换，我让豆老师跑出一份Unity中的坐标转换关系：1. 坐标系转换

视图空间与裁剪空间的转换

裁剪空间中的w分量实质上就是视线空间的z分量的相反数（小知识：如果我们把视线空间的xy分量除以裁剪空间中的w分量，得到的坐标中xy分量一定与NDC坐标成线性关系！）。

NDC空间与视图空间的转换

视线空间的z分量与NDC空间中的z分量不成线性关系，但是视线空间中的！1/z是与NDC空间中的z分量成线性关系的

屏幕空间与NDC空间的转换

从上面几个式子中可以看出来，屏幕空间z分量和视图空间1/z分量成（Unity中，经过变换之后的屏幕空间坐标的原点是在左上角，故我们应该对其进行反转），这也就是为什么我在屏幕空间插值的是1/z，而不是z。我们使用1/z可以轻松复原视图空间的z分量。线性关系

1）为什么屏幕空间要用[0, w-1]，[0, h-1]？

其实我开始看别人代码的时候想的是为什么不用[0, 1]范围的uv坐标，如果这样也方便采样，不用重新反向映射一次，直到我看到DDA算法要（float invdx = dir / deltaSS.x;），我才反应过来。实际上我们横纵范围不能看作一样的，我们屏幕分辨率是不同的（全高清1920×1080，四倍高清2560×1440 ...），想要步进屏幕空间，必须精确到像素级别！2. 重点细节讲解算1/屏幕空间增量

2）为什么循环中做一次初始半步长迈进？

从我们的相交判断条件来看：

判断rayFarZ这个较远点是否被表面遮挡；

判断rayNearZ是否在一定阈值（Thickness）内。

只有两个都满足时，才能说明相交成功，进行采样。那么我们先迈进半步长，之后的判断都在Reflection Dir方向的半步长处进行步进，如下图：

这样是十分舒服的判断，既可以防止首次的判断失误，又确保后面的判断正确！

3）为什么要这个Thickness这个阈值？

其实就是增大容错率，如下图：

1）相机向下看时，会有一个自反射圆圈，超出MaxDistance之后会消失。3. 问题解析

这个问题我仔细分析了一下，原因是在视图空间中，我们反射出来的最终位置，可能超出近裁面了，我们如果把这个点映射到屏幕空间就会出错（仔细思考MVP变换，如果有个点在你相机后面（不在视锥体内），变换之后的位置必然不在投影盒中，那么映射到屏幕空间必然会出错），所以我们必须要对这个最终反射点进行一次近裁剪面的判断，从而调整反射点的最终位置，如下：

// 视图空间中射线起始位置和结束位置

float3 startVS = posVS;

float3 endVS = posVS + reflDirVS * maxDistance;

if (endVS.z > -_ProjectionParams.y)

maxDistance = (-_ProjectionParams.y - startVS.z) / reflDirVS.z;

endVS = startVS + reflDirVS * maxDistance;

// inverse w

......

2）屏幕信息缺失

很好理解，毕竟我们在屏幕空间进行反射，那么必定会缺失信息，如下图：

根据Games 202，闫老师给的思路，在屏幕空间进行一次衰减，不同的是，闫老师的思路是利用反射距离进行衰减，我的思路是利用反射点的uv进行衰减。

那么实现步骤也是十分简单的，先在Render Pass传入一个控制衰减的参数attenuation，在Shader中，我使用暗角后处理的控制方法，如下：

if (intersecting)

{

float2 attUV = abs(hitUV - 0.5) * 1.8;

attUV = pow(saturate(attUV), attenuation);

float att = length(attUV);

float edgeFading= pow(saturate(1 - att * att), 5);

return GetSource(hitUV) * smoothness * edgeFading + GetSource(uv);

}

这个效果简单来说就是做一次屏幕边缘的衰减，我的想法就是，如果我们hitUV打到了屏幕边缘，那么就肯定给一个小的权重，若打到屏幕中心，那么肯定要给一个大点的权重，同时需要考虑到屏幕长宽的影响，综合考虑之后，我决定使用暗角作为权重。

item.title: UGUI 性能排查：隐藏血条后耗时下降，减顶点为何没改善 ｜ UGUI性能排查实战：隐藏血条后耗时下降，减少顶点为何没改善
item.description:
一句话：瓶颈是网格重建的频率而不是顶点数量；单帧 17 次物理更新其实是 Unity 的追帧上限。

要点：

  • 部分帧 UGUI 相关耗时达 20～30ms；自定义 UXImage.OnPopulateMesh 平均每帧约 77 次、峰值 259 次，CPU 5.91ms
  • 减少顶点只降低单次网格处理的数据量，并不减少重建次数，所以整体耗时可能几乎不变
  • 单帧物理更新 17 次 ≈ Fixed Timestep 0.02 秒与 Maximum Allowed Timestep 0.333 秒相除的追帧上限，先看是否集中在长帧后

为什么值得看：UI 与物理两个最容易误判的排查点：分清「重建次数」和「单次数据量」，把异常数值还原成引擎参数。

中文摘要：UWA 技术分享第 496 期整理了两个典型实战问题。第一个：隐藏血条后 UI 耗时明显下降，但减少血条顶点却没有改善——报告显示部分帧 UGUI 耗时 20～30ms，自定义 UXImage.OnPopulateMesh 平均每帧调用约 77 次、部分帧达 259 次、CPU 耗时 5.91ms，说明真正的开销是网格生成频率及其 CPU 成本，而不是顶点数量：隐藏血条同时减少了 UI 更新、网格重建与 Canvas 批次处理，而减少顶点只降低单次网格处理的数据量。排查建议是看 Graphic.Rebuild、UpdateGeometry 与自定义 OnPopulateMesh 的调用情况，检查是否存在无意义的 SetAllDirty/SetVerticesDirty 与重复赋值。第二个：单帧物理更新 17 次并不是碰撞算得太重，而是 Unity 默认 Fixed Timestep 0.02 秒与 Maximum Allowed Timestep 约 0.333 秒相除得到的追帧上限，应结合 CPU 帧耗时确认是否出现在长帧之后。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·UWA（中文）

1）隐藏血条后耗时下降，减少顶点为何没改善

2）单帧物理更新17次如何控制

这是第496篇UWA技术知识分享的推送，精选了UWA社区的热门话题，涵盖了UWA问答、社区帖子等技术知识点，助力大家更全面地掌握和学习。

UWA社区主页：

UWA QQ群：793972859

community.uwa4d.com

本次推送的实战案例来自于。UWA将关键线索、定位路径与处理建议整理成了可复用的案例笔记，便于大家快速对照、排查自身项目中的同类问题。使用UWA服务的项目的真实且典型的问题

实战案例

Q：隐藏血条后UI耗时明显下降，但减少血条顶点后没有改善，问题可能出在哪里？

A：从现有对照结果看，血条相关组件是重要的开销来源，但问题更可能出在网格生成频率及其CPU开销，而不是顶点数量。

在UWA GOT Online报告中，部分帧UGUI相关耗时达到20～30ms。隐藏血条会同时减少UI更新、网格重建及Canvas批次处理等开销；减少顶点主要降低单次网格处理的数据量，并不会减少网格重建次数，因此整体耗时可能没有明显改善。

自定义函数UXImage.OnPopulateMesh:Simple平均每帧调用约77次，部分帧达到259次，对应CPU耗时5.91ms，说明自定义UXImage的网格生成已经形成较明显的CPU开销。

不过，调用频繁不一定代表存在无效更新，也可能是大量血条在同一帧正常生成网格。排查时可以在Unity Profiler中查看Graphic.Rebuild、UpdateGeometry及自定义OnPopulateMesh的调用情况，重点检查：

是否存在不必要的SetAllDirty或SetVerticesDirty调用；

血量、填充比例和颜色没有变化时，是否仍在重复赋值；

单帧参与更新的血条数量是否符合实际需求。

如果Canvas.BuildBatch等相关耗时也较高，再评估将动态血条与静态UI分离。需要注意，拆分Canvas可以减少动态更新对其他UI的影响，但不能降低单个Graphic自身的网格生成成本。

优化后重点对比UGUI相关CPU耗时、OnPopulateMesh总耗时和网格重建次数。如果OnPopulateMesh耗时下降而UGUI总耗时变化不明显，再继续检查Canvas批次重建或其他UI更新环节。

实战案例

Q：项目运行过程中出现卡顿，UWA GOT Online报告显示部分帧的物理更新次数最高达到17次。为什么单帧会连续执行这么多次物理更新，又该如何控制？

A：单帧出现17次物理更新，不能直接判断为碰撞计算过重。这个数值更接近Unity默认参数下的物理追帧上限。

Unity默认的Fixed Timestep为0.02秒，Maximum Allowed Timestep约为0.333秒，两者相除约为16.7，因此长帧后单帧最多可能连续执行约17次物理更新。

当某一帧耗时较长时，Unity可能在后续帧连续执行多次FixedUpdate和物理模拟，用来追赶已经过去的时间。因此，需要先结合CPU帧耗时和调用时序，确认物理更新次数是否集中出现在长帧之后。

如果物理更新次数随长帧升高，说明它更可能是追帧的结果。此时应先排查造成长帧的主要开销，再决定是否限制物理追帧次数。

确认需要限制后，可以保持Fixed Timestep为0.02秒，将Maximum Allowed Timestep调整到约0.1秒。按照这组参数计算，单帧物理更新的理论上限约为5次。

降低Maximum Allowed Timestep只能限制长帧时的物理补算量，不能消除造成长帧的原始开销。参数设置过低时，严重卡顿期间的游戏时间推进会受到限制，物理模拟和FixedUpdate可能相对实际时间变慢。因此，5次只能作为测试起点，不能直接作为所有项目的通用配置。

也可以适当增大Fixed Timestep来降低物理更新频率，但这会同时影响FixedUpdate的执行频率和物理模拟精度。修改前需要确认角色移动、技能判定等逻辑是否依赖FixedUpdate。

如果限制更新次数后Physics耗时仍然偏高，再检查Overlap调用频率、检测范围、LayerMask和Layer Collision Matrix，判断单次物理计算是否过重。参数调整后，需要确认单帧FixedUpdate次数和Physics耗时确实下降，并回归角色移动、碰撞及技能判定。

无论是社区里开发者们的互助讨论，还是AI基于知识沉淀的快速反馈，核心都是为了让每一个技术难题都有解、每一次踩坑都有回响。希望这些从真实开发场景中提炼的经验，能直接帮你解决当下的技术卡点，也让你在遇到同类问题时，能更高效地找到破局方向。

封面图来源于网络

今天的分享就到这里。生有涯而知无涯，在漫漫的开发周期中，我们遇到的问题只是冰山一角，UWA社区愿伴你同行，一起探索分享。欢迎更多的开发者加入UWA社区。

UWA官网：

UWA社区：

UWA学堂：

官方技术QQ群：793972859

www.uwa4d.com

community.uwa4d.com

优化后重点对比UGUI相关CPU耗时、OnPopulateMesh总耗时和网格重建次数。如果OnPopulateMesh耗时下降而UGUI总耗时变化不明显，再继续检查Canvas批次重建或其他UI更新环节。

实战案例

Q：项目运行过程中出现卡顿，UWA GOT Online报告显示部分帧的物理更新次数最高达到17次。为什么单帧会连续执行这么多次物理更新，又该如何控制？

A：单帧出现17次物理更新，不能直接判断为碰撞计算过重。这个数值更接近Unity默认参数下的物理追帧上限。

Unity默认的Fixed Timestep为0.02秒，Maximum Allowed Timestep约为0.333秒，两者相除约为16.7，因此长帧后单帧最多可能连续执行约17次物理更新。

当某一帧耗时较长时，Unity可能在后续帧连续执行多次FixedUpdate和物理模拟，用来追赶已经过去的时间。因此，需要先结合CPU帧耗时和调用时序，确认物理更新次数是否集中出现在长帧之后。

如果物理更新次数随长帧升高，说明它更可能是追帧的结果。此时应先排查造成长帧的主要开销，再决定是否限制物理追帧次数。

确认需要限制后，可以保持Fixed Timestep为0.02秒，将Maximum Allowed Timestep调整到约0.1秒。按照这组参数计算，单帧物理更新的理论上限约为5次。

降低Maximum Allowed Timestep只能限制长帧时的物理补算量，不能消除造成长帧的原始开销。参数设置过低时，严重卡顿期间的游戏时间推进会受到限制，物理模拟和FixedUpdate可能相对实际时间变慢。因此，5次只能作为测试起点，不能直接作为所有项目的通用配置。

也可以适当增大Fixed Timestep来降低物理更新频率，但这会同时影响FixedUpdate的执行频率和物理模拟精度。修改前需要确认角色移动、技能判定等逻辑是否依赖FixedUpdate。

如果限制更新次数后Physics耗时仍然偏高，再检查Overlap调用频率、检测范围、LayerMask和Layer Collision Matrix，判断单次物理计算是否过重。参数调整后，需要确认单帧FixedUpdate次数和Physics耗时确实下降，并回归角色移动、碰撞及技能判定。

无论是社区里开发者们的互助讨论，还是AI基于知识沉淀的快速反馈，核心都是为了让每一个技术难题都有解、每一次踩坑都有回响。希望这些从真实开发场景中提炼的经验，能直接帮你解决当下的技术卡点，也让你在遇到同类问题时，能更高效地找到破局方向。

封面图来源于网络

今天的分享就到这里。生有涯而知无涯，在漫漫的开发周期中，我们遇到的问题只是冰山一角，UWA社区愿伴你同行，一起探索分享。欢迎更多的开发者加入UWA社区。

item.title: Bevy 0.20：Solari 实时路径追踪与 DLSS ｜ Bevy 0.20
item.description:
一句话：开源 Rust 引擎把实时路径追踪插件 Solari 与 DLSS 接进了主线。

要点：

  • 实时路径追踪渲染器 Solari 在几乎每个方面都做了大幅改进，并接入 DLSS
  • BSN 场景语法改进、WESL 着色器、Sprite 材质与扩展的 2D 材质
  • 更多 UI 控件与 Ready 事件，并附 0.19→0.20 迁移指南

为什么值得看：路径追踪 + 上采样这套管线已经进入开源引擎主线，Rust 引擎在渲染与着色器工具链上的追赶速度值得关注。

中文摘要：Bevy 0.20 是 Rust 数据驱动游戏引擎的中期版本，重点集中在渲染。实时路径追踪渲染器 Solari 几乎在每个方面都有明显改进，并接入了 DLSS 上采样，使路径追踪在开源引擎里第一次有了可用的性能组合。场景描述方面改进了 BSN 语法，着色器侧引入 WESL，Sprite 材质与扩展的 2D 材质补齐了 2D 工作流。此外还有更多 UI 控件与 Ready 事件等易用性改动，官方同时提供了 0.19 到 0.20 的迁移指南。对关注引擎架构的人来说，值得看的是它把路径追踪、上采样与场景语法这几块如何拆成互相独立的插件边界。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：Bevy（English）

Bevy 0.20

Posted on October 8, 2026 by Bevy Contributors

The Zorah scene rendered in Bevy Solari

Thanks to contributors, pull requests, community reviewers, and our , we're happy to announce the release on !227817

Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, has seen major improvements to pretty much every aspect of the plugin!

Read for the technical details, or continue reading below for the high level overview.

JMS55's blog

#

Thanks to improvements in our implementation, rendering is now mostly unbiased, leading to much more accurate lighting.

ReSTIR

Additionally, thanks to some other changes, moving objects no longer have shadows that lag behind, and reflections now look significantly less shimmery in motion, especially for non-metallic materials.

#

DLSS-RR has gotten very good in recent updates, and for many scenes, ReSTIR costs a decent chunk of performance, and does not significantly improve image quality.

As a result, we've decided to make ReSTIR optional, and turn it .off by default

If you were using Solari in Bevy 0.19, check if the loss of ReSTIR affects your scene, and if so re-enable .

SolariLighting::restir

With ReSTIR off, expect reduced shadow quality and missing shadows in motion in scenes with many lights. We are exploring cheaper ways of improving light sampling, without ReSTIR, to improve this in the future.

In addition, Solari's scene management code is now retained (similar to retained render world optimizations in previous versions of Bevy), and overall much more optimized, leading to reduced CPU costs.significantly

You may also want to take a look at the new fields in . While we aim to set reasonable defaults that will work well across a wide variety of games, there are now many knobs (world cache size, per-pixel light sample count, temporal accumulation, and path tracing bounce count) that can be tweaked to improve performance or quality for your specific scene, project and hardware.

SolariLighting

#

Solari now supports lighting from and s on cameras, in addition to the existing support for and emissive meshes. We're hoping to add support for the remaining , , and types .

in the near future

Solari now also runs on macOS, but note that there is currently no built-in denoiser included in for macOS. MetalFX Ray Reconstruction might be a possible solution in the future (contributions welcome!)

bevy_solari

#

Finally, our crate has been updated to support the latest version of DLSS, bringing support for DLSS-RR 4.5, which significantly improves denoising quality in Solari.

If you were using DLSS in Bevy 0.19, make sure to the newest version of the DLSS SDK, else you will run into compiler errors.

BSN landed with a few idiosyncrasies that caused friction in practice. We made some changes to BSN's syntax this cycle in the interest of improving its ergonomics and clarity. After this, the syntax largely be nailed down.should

All scene references now require prefixes:

@

// Beforebsn! { scene_variable scene_function() @SceneComponent {scene_expression}}// Afterbsn! { @scene_variable @scene_function() @SceneComponent @{scene_expression}}

template_value

You can now remove all of those pesky wrappers from your component values:

template_value

If you were using an enum that didn't support , you can now remove the wrapper:

VariantDefaults

template_value

The removal of does mean that enums must now have every field specified:

VariantDefaults

We believe this tradeoff is worth it, as it increases BSN's compatibility with arbitrary Rust enums. Rust doesn't support "enum variant defaults" anyway!

#

The "builder pattern" (and chained methods generally) previously required a wrapper. This can now be removed:

// Beforebsn! { template_value(Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y))}// Afterbsn! { Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y)}

template_value

In general, you should now be able to remove all instances from your BSN declarations!

template_value

BSN previously used commas to separate entities, with optional around entities to make the boundaries clearer. This resulted in a lot of syntax noise, line noise, and over-indentation:

()

bsn! { Node Children [ ( #OkButton @button("Ok") ), ( #CancelButton @button("Cancel") ), ]}

To avoid this, many developers opted for this syntax instead, which made it very hard to visually distinguish entities:

bsn! { Node Children [ #OkButton @button("Ok"), #CancelButton @button("Cancel"), ]}

BSN now uses to separate entities in a list:

--

bsn! { Node Children [ #OkButton @button("Ok") -- #CancelButton @button("Cancel") ]}

This gives us the best of all worlds: entities are visually distinct, and there is no over-indentation, line noise, or syntax noise ( when compared to other competitors in the "markup format" space are very competitive!). Both and have been deprecated in this context.

We landed BSN, Bevy's next generation scene system, . It was missing a key piece though: the ability to easily run logic when a scene is fully "ready" and spawned (ex: all dependencies have loaded, the full hierarchy is present, and all of the initial components are inserted in the scene). This is a critical piece for building cohesive, standalone, composable scenes. It is also necessary to properly layer Bevy logic on top of scene representations (like glTF).

in our last release

other

The closest we had was the event for a given component, which runs "top down" (meaning children are not available). We needed a "bottom up" equivalent to enable building logic that relies on the complete loaded and spawned scene.

Add

The solution is pretty straightforward: trigger a new event for each entity in a spawned scene the full spawn logic has run for that entity (including its descendants).

#[derive(SceneComponent, Default, Clone)]struct Widget;impl Widget { fn scene() -> impl Scene { bsn! { Node { width: px(100), height: px(100) } on(|ready: On<Ready>| { info!("The full scene, including 'widget.bsn' contents, is available here") }) Children [ Text("hello") -- :"widget.bsn" ] } }}world.spawn(bsn! { @Widget })

WESL

WESL is a language standard that extends WGSL to add important usability features like modules, imports, conditional compilation, and more. You can see what that looks like (and render pretty shader toys!) live in your browser in the .

WESL Playground

Bevy has historically handled these things in our own custom WGSL dialect, but we believe it is better for the wider shader ecosystem (and for us) to adopt a common standard where we can pool resources on language improvements, module ecosystems, and IDE tooling. We've been working closely with the WESL team to evolve the standard in a way that fits well into the Bevy picture.

A critical part of that tooling is language server protocol support, in the form of . That means syntax highlighting, go-to-definition, inlay hints, code folding, formatting and more, once installed for your IDE of choice.

#25128

Ordering large groups of systems with is convenient, but it can be overly strict. If system set is chained before system set , every system in must finish before system in can start, even when the systems involved never touch the same data. This often leaves worker threads idle while they wait for a handful of stragglers at the end of a system set, a pattern that shows up frequently in the render world.

.chain()

X

Y

X

any

Y

The new , , and functions provide a looser alternative. Like their regular counterparts, they request an ordering between successive elements, however that ordering is only kept between systems whose data accesses actually conflict. Systems that don't conflict are left unordered and may run in any order, including in parallel.

chain_weak()

before_weak()

after_weak()

schedule.configure_sets( ( ExtractCommands, PrepareMeshes, CreateViews, Specialize, PrepareViews, Queue, PhaseSort, Prepare, Render, Cleanup, PostCleanup, ) .chain_weak(),);

When two weakly-ordered systems actually conflict on their data access, a normal ordering is kept between them, so the earlier one still runs first. Two systems that conflict only through a non-conflicting system between them in the chain stay ordered as well. Non-conflicting systems, however, are left free to run in any order and overlap for increased parallelism!

Two kinds of system are treated as always conflicting, so their ordering is always kept: an earlier system that produces deferred effects such as (so the later system observes them, with an sync point inserted as usual), and exclusive systems (which cannot overlap anything regardless).

Commands

ApplyDeferred

Because the scheduler can only see accesses it tracks, dependencies expressed through interior mutability on read-only accesses, global state, or other untracked methods are respected. Use only when your systems don't rely on such hidden ordering, otherwise stick with .not

Components can now opt-in to "column summary change ticks":

#[derive(Component)]#[component(summary_tick)]struct MyComponent { /* fields here */}

When enabled, this will store a "column change tick" in addition to a "per-entity change tick", which allows cheaply skipping the whole column of entities when querying for changes, rather than needing to check every entity's component to see if it has changed.

This makes mutations more expensive, as they need to write both the column change tick and the entity change tick, but for entities whose changes are queried often, but change infrequently, this tradeoff can easily be worth it! Before a schedule runs (and therefore, your systems), it first computes the system run order based on their ordering constraints (, , ) and system sets. However, in addition to this, the schedule must also resolve - if system A and system B both mutate component C, and there's no ordering between A and B, the schedule needs to pick one to run first. So far, the rule has been that this is non-deterministic.

一句话：开源 Rust 引擎把实时路径追踪插件 Solari 与 DLSS 接进了主线。

要点：

  • 实时路径追踪渲染器 Solari 在几乎每个方面都做了大幅改进，并接入 DLSS
  • BSN 场景语法改进、WESL 着色器、Sprite 材质与扩展的 2D 材质
  • 更多 UI 控件与 Ready 事件，并附 0.19→0.20 迁移指南

为什么值得看：路径追踪 + 上采样这套管线已经进入开源引擎主线，Rust 引擎在渲染与着色器工具链上的追赶速度值得关注。

中文摘要：Bevy 0.20 是 Rust 数据驱动游戏引擎的中期版本，重点集中在渲染。实时路径追踪渲染器 Solari 几乎在每个方面都有明显改进，并接入了 DLSS 上采样，使路径追踪在开源引擎里第一次有了可用的性能组合。场景描述方面改进了 BSN 语法，着色器侧引入 WESL，Sprite 材质与扩展的 2D 材质补齐了 2D 工作流。此外还有更多 UI 控件与 Ready 事件等易用性改动，官方同时提供了 0.19 到 0.20 的迁移指南。对关注引擎架构的人来说，值得看的是它把路径追踪、上采样与场景语法这几块如何拆成互相独立的插件边界。

For those who don't know, Bevy is a refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust. You can check out our to try it today. It's free and open source forever! You can grab the full on GitHub. Check out for a collection of community-developed plugins, games, and learning resources.

Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, has seen major improvements to pretty much every aspect of the plugin!

Read for the technical details, or continue reading below for the high level overview.

JMS55's blog

#

Thanks to improvements in our implementation, rendering is now mostly unbiased, leading to much more accurate lighting.

ReSTIR

Additionally, thanks to some other changes, moving objects no longer have shadows that lag behind, and reflections now look significantly less shimmery in motion, especially for non-metallic materials.

#

DLSS-RR has gotten very good in recent updates, and for many scenes, ReSTIR costs a decent chunk of performance, and does not significantly improve image quality.

As a result, we've decided to make ReSTIR optional, and turn it .off by default

If you were using Solari in Bevy 0.19, check if the loss of ReSTIR affects your scene, and if so re-enable .

SolariLighting::restir

With ReSTIR off, expect reduced shadow quality and missing shadows in motion in scenes with many lights. We are exploring cheaper ways of improving light sampling, without ReSTIR, to improve this in the future.

In addition, Solari's scene management code is now retained (similar to retained render world optimizations in previous versions of Bevy), and overall much more optimized, leading to reduced CPU costs.significantly

You may also want to take a look at the new fields in . While we aim to set reasonable defaults that will work well across a wide variety of games, there are now many knobs (world cache size, per-pixel light sample count, temporal accumulation, and path tracing bounce count) that can be tweaked to improve performance or quality for your specific scene, project and hardware.

SolariLighting

#

Solari now supports lighting from and s on cameras, in addition to the existing support for and emissive meshes. We're hoping to add support for the remaining , , and types .

in the near future

Solari now also runs on macOS, but note that there is currently no built-in denoiser included in for macOS. MetalFX Ray Reconstruction might be a possible solution in the future (contributions welcome!)

bevy_solari

Finally, our crate has been updated to support the latest version of DLSS, bringing support for DLSS-RR 4.5, which significantly improves denoising quality in Solari.

If you were using DLSS in Bevy 0.19, make sure to the newest version of the DLSS SDK, else you will run into compiler errors.

BSN landed with a few idiosyncrasies that caused friction in practice. We made some changes to BSN's syntax this cycle in the interest of improving its ergonomics and clarity. After this, the syntax largely be nailed down.should

#

All scene references now require prefixes:

@

// Beforebsn! { scene_variable scene_function() @SceneComponent {scene_expression}}// Afterbsn! { @scene_variable @scene_function() @SceneComponent @{scene_expression}}

In addition to making it easier to spot scene inclusions (and unifying the syntax across cases), this freed us up to make component values easier to work with!much

You can now remove all of those pesky wrappers from your component values:

If you were using an enum that didn't support , you can now remove the wrapper:

VariantDefaults

template_value

// Beforebsn! { template_value(Foo::A)}// Afterbsn! { Foo::A}

The removal of does mean that enums must now have every field specified:

VariantDefaults

We believe this tradeoff is worth it, as it increases BSN's compatibility with arbitrary Rust enums. Rust doesn't support "enum variant defaults" anyway!

The "builder pattern" (and chained methods generally) previously required a wrapper. This can now be removed:

In general, you should now be able to remove all instances from your BSN declarations!

template_value

BSN previously used commas to separate entities, with optional around entities to make the boundaries clearer. This resulted in a lot of syntax noise, line noise, and over-indentation:

()

To avoid this, many developers opted for this syntax instead, which made it very hard to visually distinguish entities:

bsn! { Node Children [ #OkButton @button("Ok"), #CancelButton @button("Cancel"), ]}

BSN now uses to separate entities in a list:

bsn! { Node Children [ #OkButton @button("Ok") -- #CancelButton @button("Cancel") ]}

This gives us the best of all worlds: entities are visually distinct, and there is no over-indentation, line noise, or syntax noise ( when compared to other competitors in the "markup format" space are very competitive!). Both and have been deprecated in this context.

It was missing a key piece though: the ability to easily run logic when a scene is fully "ready" and spawned (ex: all dependencies have loaded, the full hierarchy is present, and all of the initial components are inserted in the scene). WESL is a language standard that extends WGSL to add important usability features like modules, imports, conditional compilation, and more. You can see what that looks like (and render pretty shader toys!) live in your browser in the .

Bevy has historically handled these things in our own custom WGSL dialect, but we believe it is better for the wider shader ecosystem (and for us) to adopt a common standard where we can pool resources on language improvements, module ecosystems, and IDE tooling. We've been working closely with the WESL team to evolve the standard in a way that fits well into the Bevy picture.
